research.area: R1: macOS host capture and pacing (ScreenCaptureKit, thread C pacing, Mac timers and power)
research.summary:
Today the Mac host does this. ScreenCaptureKit (SCK) streams one display, scaled on the GPU to the encoder's size, as an IOSurface in NV12 (sRGB, BT.709 matrix, video range) with no pointer (capture.rs:285-318). The serial SCK queue targets the user-interactive global queue (capture.rs:386-390). It keeps only the newest Complete picture, drops Idle and other statuses (capture.rs:97-148), and wakes thread C through a kqueue user event. Thread C waits on a NOTE_CRITICAL kqueue timer that the kernel does not coalesce (waiter.rs). It paces on the even grid (pacer.rs:36-39) and keeps the tick armed when nothing is fresh (video.rs:85-120). It hands the IOSurface without a copy to an asynchronous low-latency VideoToolbox session (encoder.rs:449-497).

Against airhand, pb-mapper is already equal or better on several points: zero-copy, the critical timers (airhand uses thread::sleep and a condvar), the asynchronous encode (airhand blocks in complete_frames), and the 10% interval margin.

It is behind airhand in five ways:
1. SCK's minimumFrameInterval is 0.9/max_fps, from the viewer's refresh, set once at start (capture.rs:363-367; video.rs:66). It ignores the host's own refresh and the QoS pace. SCK documents this property as the minimum time between frame updates, and frames land on vsyncs. So a 60 Hz viewer of a 144 Hz Mac (this Mac's display reads 144.0 Hz) can get at most 48 fps, a 75 Hz Mac 37.5 fps and a 165 Hz Mac 55 fps.
2. The grid never moves toward SCK arrivals. airhand anchors its timeline on the SCK timestamp (pace.rs:43-49; capture/sck.rs:246-249).
3. A display that slept without locking is never woken. airhand wakes it (power.rs:235-252).
4. Every verify does a 48 µs CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary round trip, measured here with ctypes. That is about 250 to 500 calls a second, two per capture, two per cursor sample and one per input. airhand checks the lock every 500 ms.
5. SCK keeps composing frames that thread C never takes: above the pace, and while every viewer is paused.

candidates.title: Set ScreenCaptureKit's frame interval from the host display's refresh rate, so high-refresh Macs reach the requested frame rate
candidates.airhand_evidence: airhand sets minimumFrameInterval = 1/fps (client/src-tauri/src/host/capture/sck.rs:142-144, 179). It thins faster sources in its own pacer, and its tests assume SCK delivers at the set rate on 120, 144 and 240 Hz (pace.rs:106-119). It does not account for refresh either, so the idea here is pb-mapper's own; airhand's updateConfiguration path (host/sck.rs:181-186) is reused by R1-sck-interval-follows-pace.
candidates.pb_current: Stream::start sets minimumFrameInterval = 9/(10*fps) (crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/capture.rs:363-367). fps is limits.max_fps (platform/macos/video.rs:66), which is the viewer's display refresh up to 120, or the user's choice from 30 to 120 (src/video.rs:74-92). The host display's refresh is never read: geometry() copies the mode but keeps only sizes (platform/macos/desktop.rs:70-86). The header documents the property as 'the desired minimum time in seconds between frame updates' (objc2-screen-capture-kit 0.3.2 SCStream.rs:404). Frames come at display refreshes, so a 15 ms minimum on a 144 Hz display (6.94 ms vsyncs) admits every third vsync, 20.8 ms apart.
candidates.protocol: none
candidates.expected_effect:
This is a model of SCK's documented gating over vsync-aligned frames, written in this session as a Python simulation, not measured. Most frames per second SCK delivers, before and after:
- 60 fps viewer: 144 Hz host 48 → 72; 165 Hz 55 → 82.5; 100 Hz 50 → 100; 90 Hz 45 → 90; 75 Hz 37.5 → 75. Thread C then thins each to the pace, so up to 60 frames per second reach the viewer where today it gets 37.5 to 55.
- 120 fps viewer: 144 Hz 72 → 144; 165 Hz 82.5 → 165, so a Smooth or 120 fps session gets up to 120 instead of 72 or 82.5.
- A user's own 45 fps: on a 60 Hz Mac 30 → 60 frames delivered, so the pace of 45 is met; on 120 Hz 40 → 60.
- No change on 60, 120 or 240 Hz hosts at 60 or 120 fps.
- Motion on a high-refresh Mac stops juddering at an unrequested 48 fps.
candidates.measure:
Before and after on a Mac with a non-multiple refresh. This Mac's own display is 144 Hz at 4096x2304 (read here through CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate), so it is the device once Screen Recording is granted to the terminal.
1. `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture sck_cadence` with a full-screen animation at the display's refresh running.
2. `cargo build --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --example deployed`, then `target/release/examples/deployed APP_CONFIG_PATH OUT/<arm>-<n> selftest 40 --tcp --feedback-log --fps 60`, and again with `--fps 120 --quality smooth --fps-override`. Compare presented FPS and unique fps medians, alternating the arms (A B B A).
3. The pure cadence tests run here in `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`.
Record the environment under docs/benchmarks/.
candidates.risk:
- When refresh/fps is not an integer (for example 72 frames at 144 Hz for 60 fps), SCK delivers more than the pace and thread C thins it. That already happens for 120 Hz viewers on 120 Hz Macs. It costs some GPU work for frames that are dropped.
- A ProMotion or adaptive-sync display reports its highest refresh. At an intermediate actual refresh the result is the same as today or better.
- A refresh change in the middle of a session without a size change keeps the old interval until the next rebuild. R1-sck-interval-follows-pace re-reads the refresh.
- If SCK frames were not vsync-aligned there would be no gain, but no loss either: the new interval never makes deliveries fall below the target.

candidates.title: Wake a sleeping, unlocked host display when a viewer's capture starts or finds no picture
candidates.airhand_evidence:
- Commit 0ae6f23 says ScreenCaptureKit cannot capture a sleeping display: the controller sees black or a capture failure, and connecting does not wake it.
- airhand wakes the display with IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity(kIOPMUserActiveLocal), at most once every 2 s (client/src-tauri/src/host/power.rs:22-31, 163, 235-252).
- It does so at session start (session.rs:476-482) and whenever capture finds CGDisplayIsAsleep, then retries (capture/sck.rs:150-161, 268-272).
candidates.change:
1. New platform/macos/power.rs:
   - extern "C" IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity(CFStringRef, u32, *mut u32) -> i32 and IOPMAssertionRelease, linked with #[link(name = "IOKit", kind = "framework")], following the ApplicationServices extern in desktop.rs:23-28;
   - `pub(crate) fn wake(id: CGDirectDisplayID) -> bool`: when `CGDisplayIsAsleep(id)` (objc2-core-graphics CGDisplayConfiguration.rs:254; feature already on), declare kIOPMUserActiveLocal activity at most once every 2 s. A static parking_lot Mutex<(Option<Instant>, u32)> keeps the time and reuses the assertion id, which is released in timers::release (timer.rs:43-53).
2. platform/macos/video.rs:
   - MacVideo::open (50-74) calls power::wake(display.id) before Stream::start. MacDesktop::prepare has already passed inside capture_video (native.rs:187-190), so a locked Mac stays SecureDesktop and is never lit.
   - In submit's no-picture failure (96-103), when wake() reports the display asleep, fail with 'the display is asleep; waking it'. The 200 ms retry then reopens once the display is lit.
3. A pure unit test of the once-per-2-s rule.
4. Docs: the macOS hosting paragraph, and a CHANGELOG bullet.
candidates.protocol: none
candidates.expected_effect: A Mac whose display slept without locking gets a picture instead of a session that never shows one. This covers no password after display sleep, or a delay longer than the sleep (typical of an always-on Mac mini used as a host). It also covers a viewer resuming after a long pause, during which the guard was released and the display slept. airhand's notes suggest the picture appears about 1 to 2 s after connecting (an estimate). The 200 ms stream-rebuild loop this case causes today goes away with it.
candidates.measure: Device: on the host, set 'Require password after the display is turned off' to a delay longer than the test, run `pmset displaysleepnow`, then connect with `target/release/examples/deployed APP_CONFIG_PATH OUT/<arm> selftest 30 --tcp --feedback-log`. Before: repeated desktop_capture failures ('delivered no picture') and no presented frame. After: time to first presented frame, read from the feedback log. Also run with 'immediately' to confirm a locked Mac still reports the secure desktop and stays dark.
candidates.risk:
- It lights a display the owner let sleep, which is expected when a viewer was accepted. A locked Mac is untouched, because the secure-desktop check runs first.
- An IOKit link adds a system framework. Its symbols exist on every macOS the app supports.
- A closed MacBook with only its built-in panel is not in the active display list, so it is not reached.

candidates.title: Anchor thread C's pacing on ScreenCaptureKit arrivals (E phase 2, Mac part)
candidates.airhand_evidence:
- airhand's pacer timeline follows each picture's timestamp. It takes a picture up to a quarter period early, moves at most 1/64 period earlier per frame, and restarts after a stall (client/src-tauri/src/host/pace.rs:1-11, 34-49).
- The stamp is the SCK presentation time converted to an Instant (capture/sck.rs:246-249; macos.rs:327-334; clock.rs:29-40).
- pacer.done(captured) is called per frame (capture/mod.rs:617-620).
candidates.pb_current:
- Pacer::consume sets next = max(next + period, now + 3/4 period) whatever the picture's time (pacer.rs:36-39). capture_at waits for pacer.next() whenever a fresh picture is Ready (worker/capture.rs:170-191).
- Latest carries no time (platform/macos/capture.rs:75-81, 138-144). The encoder's pts is the submit time (encoder.rs:457).
- When the host display delivers at, or slightly above, the delivered rate, every arrival lands a little before the grid tick, and the wait grows each frame to a full period. When the wait exceeds a source period, a picture is dropped.
- E's research designed the fix (scratchpad research/E-capture-pacing.json, design A-D). Only phase 1 (armed ticks for Windows) shipped.
candidates.protocol: none (a provided method on the SDK's Backend trait; no wire, ALPN or helper change)
candidates.expected_effect:
These figures are a model: a Python simulation in this session with ±0.3 ms arrival jitter over 120 s, not measured. Today's grid against the anchored pacer:
- 60 Hz display 100 ppm fast, pace 60: mean wait 3.4 ms, p95 8.4 ms, and growing toward about 8 ms mean over longer sessions → 0.
- 60.05 Hz: mean 7.7 ms, max 16.6 ms, 5 dropped pictures per 2 min → 0, none dropped.
- A 120 Hz display delivering every second frame at pace 60 behaves the same: 3.4 → 0.
- Displays slower than the pace are already at 0.
About half of hosts (displays whose clock runs fast against mach time) gain roughly 3 to 8 ms of latency in continuous motion and lose the periodic dropped frame. Together with R1-sck-interval-follows-pace, pace 30 on a 60 Hz Mac goes from a phase-dependent 3.4 to 13.7 ms (8.3 ms mean over phases) to 0.
candidates.measure:
- Here: `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features` (new pacer and worker tests), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, and `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`.
- Device, with Screen Recording: `deployed APP_CONFIG_PATH OUT/<arm>-<n> selftest 40 --tcp --feedback-log`, with a 60 fps animation on 60 Hz and 120 Hz host displays, in the order A B B A. Compare desktop_capture_wait median and p95 and the dropped-picture count, and check presented FPS is unchanged.
- host_send_bench must show no allocation change per frame, since the data path is touched.
candidates.risk:
- Documented rule 2 ('even grid') is reworded. Its guarantees stay: skips only for backpressure, no catch-up burst (the 3/4 floor), and the long-run rate is kept.
- A source whose presents land early can run up to 1/64 above the pace.
- Windows keeps the grid until it supplies stamps (another area).
- Thread C's Clock under Manual mixes domains with real platform stamps, so only the Fake dates its pictures in tests.

candidates.title: Retune ScreenCaptureKit's interval live to the QoS pace, so SCK stops composing frames thread C never takes
candidates.airhand_evidence:
- airhand sets SCK's interval from the highest fps among its subscribers, and updates it live with updateConfiguration whenever that fps changes (capture/mod.rs:470-479, 603-608; capture/sck.rs:318-324; host/sck.rs:181-186).
- It stops the stream when the last subscriber goes (capture/mod.rs:505-515).
candidates.pb_current:
- SCK runs at the viewer's max_fps for the stream's life (video.rs:66; capture.rs:363-367).
- The QoS pace is lower in common cases: the Balanced ceiling of 60 under a 120 Hz viewer, the Quality ceiling of 30 (qos.rs:101-123), the 15×scale startup cap, congestion, and the viewer's cap (qos.rs:590-610).
- MacVideo::set_rate receives VideoRate{bitrate, pace_fps} on every capture (native.rs:212-216; worker/capture.rs:315-318) but ignores pace_fps (video.rs:78-81).
- Each surplus frame is scaled and converted by WindowServer and the GPU, and wakes thread C (capture.rs:138-147), only to be replaced.
candidates.protocol: none
candidates.risk:
- updateConfiguration is asynchronous, so the first frames after a rise in pace come at the old rate.
- A larger interval relies on SCK delivering a throttled change at the next allowed vsync rather than dropping it. Today's 15 ms gating has no reported lost final frames, which suggests it defers. The device run must confirm that a final change (the end of a scroll) arrives.

candidates.title: Reuse the Mac session and geometry check for 10 ms instead of a 48 µs WindowServer round trip per verify
candidates.airhand_evidence: airhand reads CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary for the lock state only every 500 ms (STATE_CHECK, capture/sck.rs:46, 268-284; macos.rs:308-314), and never per input.
candidates.pb_current:
- PlatformBackend::verify calls MacDesktop::prepare and then display_matches (native.rs:92-100).
- prepare reads CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary plus two key lookups (desktop.rs:120-142, 206-208). display_matches reads CGDisplayBounds and CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode (desktop.rs:70-86, 185-200, 213-216).
- Measured here (M6, ctypes): 48.0 µs, 5.8 µs and 5.4 µs per call.
- verify runs twice per capture (native.rs:188, 217). On a Mac the second check says nothing about a picture SCK captured earlier.
- It runs twice per cursor sample, every 16 ms (native.rs:255-265; worker/cursor.rs:11), and once per input (native.rs:276-281).
candidates.protocol: none
candidates.measure:
- Here: `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture session_check`, before and after (µs per verify).
- Device: `sample <host pid> 10` during `deployed ... selftest 40 --tcp` with the pointer moving, before and after; compare the share of CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary and thread C CPU (`top -l 20 -stats pid,cpu,th`).
candidates.risk:
- A lock or a fast-user switch reaches the injection path up to 10 ms later. The 100 ms context check is unchanged, and the codebase already reuses a helper answer for 4 ms.
- A display-mode change is seen up to 10 ms later on the capture path. The context check and SCK still catch it.

candidates.title: Slow ScreenCaptureKit to 2 frames a second while every viewer is paused
candidates.airhand_evidence:
- airhand stops a display's capture when its last subscriber goes (capture/mod.rs:505-515).
- It lowers SCK's interval to the subscribers' fps live (capture/sck.rs:318-324).
candidates.pb_current:
- When every slot is paused (a hidden viewer window, a backgrounded phone app), thread C only drains and marks a keyframe (worker/capture.rs:235-261).
- MacVideo and its SCK stream keep running at max_fps. Every change on the host is still composed and scaled on the GPU into the Latest slot that nobody takes.
- The timer guard and its NSActivity are released meanwhile (worker.rs:872-878), so nothing else changes.
candidates.change:
1. backend.rs: a provided `fn video_paused(&mut self, paused: bool) {}`. Forward it in Box, PlatformBackend, NativeBackend, RemoteBackend and guarded.rs.
2. worker/capture.rs calls it on the transition into the all-paused branch (235) and out of it (262).
3. platform/mod.rs VideoSource gets a provided `fn paused(&mut self, paused: bool) {}`. PlatformBackend forwards it to the open source.
4. MacVideo implements it through Stream::set_interval (from R1-sck-interval-follows-pace): 500 ms while paused, and the pace interval on resume.
5. The resume IDR still comes from Latest at once, as today.
6. A worker test that the hook fires once per transition.
candidates.protocol: none
candidates.expected_effect: An estimate; the GPU cost per frame is unmeasured. While every viewer is paused and the host shows motion (a video, an animation), SCK composes at most 2 frames a second instead of 60 to 120. Nothing changes on a still screen or for a live viewer. Resume is as fast as today.
candidates.measure:
Device: hide the viewer during `deployed ... serve` (or pause the selftest) with a moving source. Compare SCK callbacks/s (debug counter), `sudo powermetrics --samplers gpu_power` and WindowServer CPU, before and after.
Correctness gate: change the content during the pause and then stop; resume within 2 s; the viewer must show the final content.
candidates.risk: - If SCK dropped throttled updates instead of deferring them, the resume IDR could show a picture up to 500 ms stale until the next change. The correctness gate decides. The fallback is to stop the stream after 5 s of pause and restart it on resume, which costs the start time.

candidates.title: Start and restart ScreenCaptureKit without enumerating every window
candidates.airhand_evidence: airhand looks up the display with getShareableContentExcludingDesktopWindows:false onScreenWindowsOnly:true (client/src-tauri/src/host/sck.rs:107-111), so off-screen windows are not enumerated.
candidates.pb_current:
- Every Stream::start calls display(id) (capture.rs:358).
- display(id) runs SCShareableContent.getShareableContentWithCompletionHandler (capture.rs:224-253), which lists every window of every app, off-screen ones included, while thread C blocks for up to 5 s.
- This happens at session start, on every rebuild (configure_video drops the source, native.rs:151-156), and on every 200 ms retry while unavailable.
- The still path already caches its filter per display (still.rs:21-38); the video path does not.
candidates.change:
1. capture.rs display(id) calls `getShareableContentExcludingDesktopWindows_onScreenWindowsOnly_completionHandler(true, true, ..)` (objc2-screen-capture-kit SCShareableContent.rs:281); only displays are read.
2. The SCContentFilter is cached per display id for the session, as SckStill does:
   - hold it in ScreenAccess (mod.rs:85), the Grant every MacVideo::open receives, behind a Mutex with a Send wrapper like ShareableContent (capture.rs:170-172);
   - drop it on any stream start failure or a DisplayLost.
3. A debug event times display(id) and start → first Complete frame.
candidates.protocol: none
candidates.expected_effect: An estimate: the time to the first picture at connect, after a resolution or codec change, and on each recovery retry drops by the window-enumeration time. That is tens of ms on a typical Mac and more with many windows (unmeasured). The retry loop's CPU falls with it.
candidates.measure: Device with Screen Recording, 30 or more windows open: compare the new debug event's enumeration ms and start-to-first-frame ms, and the selftest's time to first presented frame, before and after, 10 connects each.
candidates.risk: A cached filter for a display reconfigured in place could fail to start a stream. Dropping the cache on failure falls back to a fresh lookup on the next retry.

candidates.title: Let ScreenCaptureKit fill the encoder's frame instead of letterboxing a sub-pixel strip
candidates.airhand_evidence: airhand sets setPreservesAspectRatio(false) on macOS 14+ because the even-rounded encode size differs from the display's aspect by under a pixel: fill, no black edge (client/src-tauri/src/host/capture/sck.rs:172-175).
candidates.pb_current:
- configuration() keeps SCK's default preservesAspectRatio = true (capture.rs:285-318; the header documents the default at SCStream.rs:442).
- scaled_size rounds to even sizes and may lose one source edge pixel (qos.rs scaled_size).
- So SCK letterboxes up to about a pixel. Since #57 (commit 908a718) that strip is opaque black ('what the display's picture does not cover'). The picture is shrunk by that amount, while viewers map pointer positions across the whole frame.
candidates.change: In configuration() (capture.rs:285-318), on macOS 14 and later, when `SCStreamConfiguration::class().responds_to(sel!(setPreservesAspectRatio:))` (the pattern at 307-309), call setPreservesAspectRatio(false). Keep the black background for older systems. Extend capture_without_a_pointer_stays_opaque (platform/macos/tests.rs:227-258) to assert the flag where the selector exists. Stills use the same configuration and gain too.
candidates.protocol: none
candidates.expected_effect: No black or half-black line along an edge of the remote picture when the encode size's aspect differs from the display's (for example 3024x1964 into 1662x1080). The stretch is at most 0.1%, which cannot be seen. Pointer mapping becomes exact.
candidates.measure: Device: log SCStreamFrameInfoContentRect (SCStream.rs:813-818) for a 3024x1964 or similar display captured to 1662x1080, before (a rect short of the frame) and after (the full frame). Inspect the last row and column of a `deployed` thumbnail.
candidates.risk: None found. On macOS 12.3 to 13 behaviour is unchanged.

not_worth_it.title: airhand's dedicated capture thread that paces with thread::sleep and waits on a condvar inbox (capture/mod.rs:558-631; capture/sck.rs:292-305)
not_worth_it.reason: pb-mapper's single thread C already waits on a NOTE_CRITICAL kqueue timer (platform/macos/waiter.rs), which the kernel does not coalesce. A condvar or sleep wait was measured 5.5 to 107 ms late on a Mac CI runner (docs/remote-desktop.md, 'Timers on a Mac host'). A second thread would add a hop and lose that.

not_worth_it.title: Raising capture and encode threads to QOS_CLASS_USER_INTERACTIVE (macos.rs:336-341; capture/mod.rs:729-739)
not_worth_it.reason: This was withdrawn after measurement: thread C at user-interactive showed no gain under an all-core load on this Mac (docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-desktop-pipeline). The SCK queue already targets the user-interactive global queue (capture.rs:386-390). Nothing in this design removes that measured result.

not_worth_it.title: minimumFrameInterval of exactly 1/fps (capture/sck.rs:142-144, 179)
not_worth_it.reason: Vsync-aligned frame times on a 60 Hz display sit right at 16.67 ms, so an exact 1/60 can halve the rate. pb-mapper's 10% margin exists for that. Both are superseded by R1-sck-refresh-interval.

not_worth_it.title: queueDepth 7 (capture/sck.rs:51)
not_worth_it.reason: pb-mapper's 6 is asserted at least ENCODER_DEPTH + 2 (capture.rs:46-52; worker.rs:80). There is no evidence of surface starvation, and one more IOSurface per stream is memory with nothing to gain.

not_worth_it.title: The SCK presentation timestamp as the frame's capture time for audio/video sync (capture/sck.rs:246-249; clock.rs)
not_worth_it.reason: pb-mapper has no audio. For pacing, the arrival time is what thread C can act on. The display time is read only for diagnostics in R1-mac-anchored-pacing. Encoder pts from submit time is what VideoToolbox budgets by, as airhand also does (vt.rs:417-418).

not_worth_it.title: showsCursor for a game mode (capture/sck.rs:177-178)
not_worth_it.reason: pb-mapper draws the pointer on the viewer and has no relative-pointer mode. Drawing it into the video would make every pointer move a full-frame encode.

not_worth_it.title: Layout check every 2 s and rebuilding the stream on lock or unlock every 500 ms (capture/sck.rs:262-284)
not_worth_it.reason: pb-mapper is already stricter. It checks the context every 100 ms (worker.rs:81). MacDesktop::prepare fails on a lock and drops the video source (native.rs:83-89; desktop.rs:120-142), so the stream is rebuilt after an unlock.

not_worth_it.title: Capturing and controlling the lit lock screen, and the lid-closed virtual display (commits 0ae6f23, 561d54e; virtual_display/mac.rs)
not_worth_it.reason: These are features, not performance. pb-mapper deliberately treats a locked Mac as the secure desktop (desktop.rs:118-150). Changing that needs its own security design.

not_worth_it.title: PreventSystemSleep and PreventUserIdleSystemSleep assertions and the 'Prevent automatic sleeping' menu (power.rs:20-45)
not_worth_it.reason: These keep a host available; they do not speed anything up. While capturing, pb-mapper's activity already disables idle display sleep (timer.rs:28-41). Waking a sleeping display, the part that affects sessions, is taken as R1-mac-wake-display.

not_worth_it.title: Static refinement: re-encode the last frame up to 8 times 200 ms after motion stops (pipeline.rs:11-14, 35-40)
not_worth_it.reason: This is an encoder-quality idea from area H, not capture pacing. Its value on a Mac depends on VideoToolbox's rate control for repeats, which H's area must measure.

not_worth_it.title: Synchronous VTCompressionSessionCompleteFrames after each frame (encoder/vt.rs:441-445)
not_worth_it.reason: pb-mapper's asynchronous output callback, which wakes thread C (encoder.rs:645-662), already avoids blocking thread C for the encoder's latency.

not_worth_it.title: Using SCK dirty rects (SCStreamFrameInfoDirtyRects)
not_worth_it.reason: airhand does not use them either. VideoToolbox has no public dirty-region or ROI input for H.264 or H.265, and SCK already sends only changed frames (Idle otherwise).

not_worth_it.title: Setting captureResolution
not_worth_it.reason: Neither project sets it, and there is no evidence the default degrades display capture. Check it during the R1-sck-fill-aspect device run rather than change it blind.

not_worth_it.title: Encoding directly in the SCK callback to skip the thread C hop
not_worth_it.reason: It would save one kqueue wake, tens of µs, but breaks thread C's single ownership of pacing, IDR, the gates and the desktop check.

not_worth_it.title: Present-anchored pacing for Windows (DXGI LastPresentTime) and its helper field
not_worth_it.reason: Out of this area. R1-mac-anchored-pacing adds the shared seam with None by default, so the Windows area can supply stamps later without changing it.

critique.area: R1: macOS host capture and pacing (ScreenCaptureKit cadence, thread C pacing, display power, session checks)

reviews.factual_errors:
1. Nobody has measured the strict vsync-gating model that every claimed gain depends on. The binding's own header (objc2-screen-capture-kit 0.3.2 SCStream.rs:405) adds 'The default value is 1/60, meaning that updates are coming in at or up to 60fps'. That shows an interval equal to the vsync period passes. It does not tell strict per-frame gating (deliver only if displayTime minus the last delivered displayTime is at least the interval) from a scheduled gate. Under a scheduled gate, today's 15 ms already delivers about 66 frames a second at 144 Hz, and the frame-rate gain disappears.
2. 'No loss' is wrong. With the floor rule (n=2 at 144 Hz for 60 fps), SCK delivers 72 frames a second and each taken picture waits for the grid tick. In this review's model (strict gating, 3 ms delivery; /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lb7666--claude-spares-spare-vPIbq7/2de9709e-ea4b-442d-a692-7f9e8fd50cdd/scratchpad/notes/r1review/latency_model.py), the time from a change on screen to its capture rises from 9.9 ms today (48 fps) to 14.8 ms. Delivering every vsync gives the same 60 fps at 11.1 ms. At 165 Hz the figures are 9.1 ms today, 14.0 ms with the floor rule and 11.0 ms every vsync.
3. The unknown-refresh fallback of 0.5/target is not a safe default. The app itself notes that a built-in panel can report 0 from CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate (ui/darwin/DesktopVideo.swift:1063). If a 120 Hz ProMotion panel reported 0, 0.5/60 would make it deliver 120 frames a second to a 60 fps viewer, where today it delivers 60. CVDisplayLink's nominal period can be read off the main thread: on this Mac it is 166667/24 MHz = 143.9997 Hz, against 144.0 from CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate. Today's 0.9/max_fps must remain the last fallback.
4. airhand's pace.rs:106-119 test thins an unthrottled 120/144/240 Hz source in airhand's own pacer. It does not model SCK delivering at the set rate; only the module comment (pace.rs:4-5) assumes that.
5. Refresh-read cost, measured here in C: CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode takes 6.2-6.5 µs (it is an IPC). That is negligible once per open.
reviews.effect_assessment:
Real only if SCK gates strictly, and then only for Macs whose refresh is not a multiple of the target: 75, 100, 144 and 165 Hz external displays. This Mac's display is 144 Hz.

Model results, all under strict gating:
- 60 fps viewer: 37.5, 50, 48 and 55 frames taken a second (75, 100, 144, 165 Hz hosts) become 60.
- 120 fps viewer: 72 at 144 Hz and 82.5 at 165 Hz become 120.
- With every-vsync delivery, a change waits about 1 to 2.5 ms longer to be captured at 144/165 Hz (+1.2 ms at 144 Hz/60, +0.7 ms at 144 Hz/120), and 2.5 to 4 ms longer at 75/100 Hz.

The rate rises from 37.5-55 to 60, or from 72-82.5 to 120. That is the effect users notice in presented FPS and smoothness. Hosts at 60, 120 or 240 Hz see no change at 60 or 120 fps. Step 0 below decides whether any of this is real.
reviews.corrected_design:
Merge this item with R1-sck-interval-follows-pace: one cadence function, used at open and on every pace change.

1. New pure module platform/macos/cadence.rs, built and tested everywhere like geometry.rs (mod.rs:18-30). `pub(crate) fn frame_interval(refresh_hz: Option<f64>, target_fps: u32, max_fps: u32) -> Duration`:
   - With a refresh: m = refresh/target. If m is within 1% of an integer k >= 1, n = k: SCK delivers at the pace, and the grid takes each picture with no wait. Otherwise n = max(1, floor(m/4)), which is every vsync for any m below 8, the lowest staleness. Interval = (n - 0.5)/refresh.
   - Without a refresh: today's 9/(10*max_fps), unchanged, and the pace is not followed.
2. Refresh source (capture.rs, OS calls only here):
   - CGDisplayModeGetRefreshRate(CGDisplayCopyDisplayMode(id)) when it is above 1;
   - else CVDisplayLinkCreateWithCGDisplay plus CVDisplayLinkGetNominalOutputVideoRefreshPeriod. This needs objc2-core-video's 'CVDisplayLink' feature in the workspace Cargo.toml, and `#[allow(deprecated)]` with the reason (the only off-main-thread source for built-in panels);
   - else None.
3. Stream::start takes the interval from frame_interval(refresh, rate.pace_fps.min(max_fps), max_fps) instead of capture.rs:363-367. Add an info event macos_capture_opened with refresh_hz, the display-link period, n and interval_us.
4. Tests in cadence.rs:
   - a table: 144/60 gives n=1, 120/60 gives n=2, 119.88/60 gives n=2, 59.94/60 gives n=1, 240/60 gives n=4, 60/25 gives n=1, 60/30 gives n=2, None gives 0.9/max;
   - a strict-gating simulator over vsync-aligned frames for refresh in {48, 59.94, 60, 75, 90, 100, 119.88, 120, 144, 165, 240} and targets 20 to 120. Assert that delivered >= min(target, refresh) * 0.99, and that at exact multiples delivered equals the target.
5. Docs: the macOS paragraph of 'Host: capture and encoding' and the constants table. Add a CHANGELOG bullet only after the device run, with measured figures.

If Step 0 shows the floor rule's GPU saving matters more than about 3 ms of latency, the fallback is n = max(1, floor(m)) for m >= 2. Choose it only from measured WindowServer and GPU numbers.

reviews.factual_errors:
1. The retry loop has two forms, not one 200 ms loop:
   - When SCK starts but delivers no Complete picture, MacVideo fails after FIRST_SUBMIT_WAIT (3 s, video.rs:96-103). geometry() had already cleared `streaming`, so fail() schedules the next try UNAVAILABLE_RETRY (200 ms) later (worker/capture.rs:106-111). The stream is rebuilt about every 3.2 s.
   - The 200 ms loop happens when SCK does not list the display: capture::display returns DisplayLost (capture.rs:246-252), and every retry repeats a full SCShareableContent enumeration.
2. The design misses that CGGetActiveDisplayList returns only awake, drawable displays. A sleeping display can therefore be absent from desktop::active() before MacVideo::open is ever reached: desktop::resolve(Device) and by_name (desktop.rs:62-66, 112-114), and MacDesktop::open's fallback (desktop.rs:163-171), fail with DisplayLost. airhand wakes at session start (session.rs:476-482) and when the display cannot be listed (capture/sck.rs:157-160), not only before opening the stream.
3. Scope: under macOS's 'Require password ... immediately', the screen locks when the display sleeps. prepare() then reports SecureDesktop and, correctly, nothing is woken. The gain is for Macs with a delay or no password after display sleep (an always-on Mac mini host), not for most laptops.
reviews.effect_assessment: Real and large where it applies. A session that today never shows a picture until someone touches the Mac shows one shortly after connecting. airhand's notes suggest 1-2 s; that is not measured. It also ends the rebuild loop. There is no effect on locked Macs (by design) or on awake displays.
reviews.corrected_design:
1. New platform/macos/power.rs:
   - extern IOPMAssertionDeclareUserActivity and IOPMAssertionRelease with #[link(name = "IOKit", kind = "framework")], following desktop.rs:23-28. objc2-io-kit's pwr_mgt module has them too, but would be a new direct crate.
   - A pure `WakeLimiter` (injected Instant): at most one declaration every 2 s.
   - `wake(ids)`: for each id where CGDisplayIsAsleep (CGDisplayConfiguration feature, already on), declare kIOPMUserActiveLocal activity, reusing the returned id as the header asks (a static Mutex<(Option<Instant>, IOPMAssertionID)>). Return whether any display was asleep.
   - Skip a built-in display (CGDisplayIsBuiltin) while the lid is closed. Read AppleClamshellState from IOPMrootDomain, as airhand does (power.rs:254-260, macos.rs lid_state): otherwise the panel lights behind the lid for about 10 s and goes dark again in a cycle.
2. Call sites, each only after desktop::available() has passed (unlocked, on the console):
   a. Macos::open (mod.rs:153), before MacDesktop::open: if any online display (CGGetOnlineDisplayList) is asleep, wake it, then poll every 100 ms for up to 3 s for the selected display to become active. This is thread C at session start, as airhand waits up to 3 s before Hello.
   b. MacVideo::open (video.rs:50-74), before Stream::start: wake(display.id).
   c. On MacVideo's no-picture failure (video.rs:96-103), or a DisplayLost from capture::display, while CGDisplayIsAsleep(id): wake it, and fail with CaptureFailed 'the display is asleep; waking it'. The 200 ms retry then reopens.

reviews.factual_errors:
1. 'About half of hosts' has no support. On Apple Silicon, mach time and the display's timing share the 24 MHz reference; CVDisplayLink reports this Mac's period as 166667 ticks of 24 MHz. So a display drifts against the grid only by how far its mode timing deviates from n × pace. The grid's period, Duration::from_secs(1)/fps truncated to the nanosecond, is never longer than nominal. Exact CTA timings (60.000, 120.000 Hz) and slow ones (59.94, CVT-RB 59.95) therefore never drift ahead of it. Only timings slightly above n × pace are affected, and their share is unknown.
2. The pace-30 gain ('3.4 to 13.7 ms to 0 together with follow-pace') comes from follow-pace alone. When SCK delivers exactly at the pace, today's grid with the armed tick already waits 0. Model (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lb7666--claude-spares-spare-vPIbq7/2de9709e-ea4b-442d-a692-7f9e8fd50cdd/scratchpad/notes/r1review/sck_model.py), 60 Hz at pace 30 with SCK following: grid 0.00, anchored 0.00. Anchoring alone, without follow-pace, cuts that case from 9.3 to 5.4 ms, and 120 Hz at pace 60 from 4.2 to 1.2 ms.
3. For a display that runs fast, the long-run mean wait tends to P/2 (8.3 ms at pace 60), once the P/4 margin left by the last re-anchor is used up. Model over 10 min: 20 ppm fast gives a mean of 2.7 ms and p95 of 7.5 ms (still rising); 100 ppm gives 7.0 ms and 15.4 ms. Anchored: 0 in both.
reviews.effect_assessment: Real for affected displays: a mean wait of up to about 8 ms, and one dropped picture per drift cycle, both go to 0. Before follow-pace's update applies, or when the refresh is unknown, it also gives the partial gains at integer multiples listed above. It is neutral when SCK delivers at a non-integer multiple of the pace (model within ±0.5 ms). How many displays are affected is unknown; the open event below measures it per display.

With a 16 ms reuse shared by capture and cursor, that drops to about 62 reads a second: about 10 ms a second saved (about 1% of a core) and about 180 fewer WindowServer IPCs a second. research.area: R2: macOS host VideoToolbox encoding (crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/{encoder.rs,video.rs}, codec/, idr.rs, qos.rs)
research.summary:
pb-mapper's VideoToolbox setup is already a superset of airhand's (airhand encoder/vt.rs:60-277). It requests low-latency rate control for both H.264 and H.265 with fallback (encoder.rs:220-247), uses Constrained High under low latency (301-309), reads back the GOP and the data-rate cap (364-390), creates the ForceKeyFrame dictionary once (392-394), and has asynchronous output with ENCODER_DEPTH 4 (worker.rs:80) and one AVCC-to-Annex-B copy from the borrowed block (618-642, 706-717). airhand instead calls CompleteFrames after every frame (vt.rs:429-445), uses low latency for H.264 only, plain High, and makes three copies. There is nothing in airhand's property set to port.

I probed real VideoToolbox on this M6 / macOS 27 with a Swift probe outside the repo (notes/vtprobe.swift; results in notes/r2-vt-measurements.txt). The machine had a load average of 2-4 from other agents, and the frames were synthetic IOSurfaces, not ScreenCaptureKit. Four findings matter:
1. The low-latency encoder (com.apple.videotoolbox.videoencoder.*.rtvc) encodes synchronously inside VTCompressionSessionEncodeFrame whenever width and height are multiples of 16. The call took 3.2 ms at 720p, 5.5 ms at 1920x1200, 7.0-12.4 ms at 2560x1440 and 7.7 ms at 2560x1600, and 16.5 ms at p95 at 4K. That blocks thread C, which also injects input, so the claims "never waits" (video.rs:82-84) and "input never waits behind encode" (worker.rs:1-5) are false at those sizes.
2. Low-latency rate control silently drops frames. After every forced IDR it drops every other frame for 0.65-1.8 s at 4 Mbit/s or less. Under budget pressure it drops 12% of frames on video-like content.
3. The speed and latency keys are refused under low latency (-12900): PrioritizeEncodingSpeedOverQuality, MaximumRealTimeFrameRate, MaxFrameDelayCount and SpatialAdaptiveQPLevel.
4. Dwell is about 5-6 ms at 1080p, 7-7.6 ms at 1440p and about 15 ms at 4K. 4K120 is therefore encoder-bound at about 66 fps on this chip.

The real wins here are:
- moving the VideoToolbox calls off thread C;
- stopping budget drops with MaxAllowedFrameQP 51;
- re-submitting a dropped final picture at the next tick instead of after 250 ms;
- aligning scaled encode sizes to multiples of 16, which removes a hidden copy.

candidates.title: Call VideoToolbox from a dedicated per-encoder submit thread so the synchronous low-latency encode never blocks thread C's input lane
candidates.airhand_evidence: airhand encodes on its own per-stream thread, named airhand-encoder-{stream} (client/src-tauri/src/host/pipeline.rs:96-98, run at 175), and injects input on a separate per-session injector thread (host/input/thread.rs:1-13, 82-96). Its synchronous VideoToolbox submit, encode_frame then complete_frames (encoder/vt.rs:416-451, 429-442), therefore never delays input.
candidates.pb_current:
Thread C does input injection and encoding in one loop: it drains the lanes, then capture_step, then drains the lanes again (worker.rs:826-860). capture_step calls backend.capture_video (worker/capture.rs:318-322), which goes through native.rs:211-217 to MacVideo::submit (video.rs:85-109) and on to Encoder::encode (encoder.rs:449-497). That calls session.encode_frame on thread C (472-481).

Measured here under low-latency rate control, the call blocks for the whole encode when width and height are multiples of 16:
- 1280x720: 3.18 ms
- 1920x1200: 5.55 ms
- 2048x1152: 5.58 ms
- 2304x1296: 5.93 ms
- 2560x1440: 6.96 ms (H.264), 7.9 ms (H.265), and 12.4 ms with default QoS under load
- 2560x1600: 7.68 ms
- 3840x2160: 0.7 ms p50, 16.5 ms p95

With the standard rate control the call returns in 0.2-0.5 ms. pb-mapper's own ignored test agrees: at 4K with low latency only 182 of 240 frames were submitted at pace 60 (scratchpad h264_run2.txt).

The docs promise input_wait p99 of 5 ms or less (docs/remote-desktop.md:1705-1711). set_bitrate (encoder.rs:410-431) also runs on thread C; it measured 0.17-0.55 ms p50 and up to 2.6 ms.
candidates.change:
In platform/macos/encoder.rs:

1. Add a `Submitter` owned by `Encoder`. It is one std::thread named `pb-mapper-vt-submit`, spawned in `Encoder::build` after `prepare_to_encode_frames` (encoder.rs:352-357). It is not spawned for the `encodes()` probe (199-215).
   - The thread owns a `CFRetained<VTCompressionSession>` clone, the prebuilt keyframe dictionary and an `Arc<Shared>` clone. A `SendSession` newtype carries them, with `unsafe impl Send` and a SAFETY note: CF retain and release are atomic, and VideoToolbox accepts calls from any thread when they are serialised. capture.rs:349-353 uses the same pattern.

2. Add a job queue to `State` (encoder.rs:58-73): a `VecDeque<Job>` with `with_capacity(ENCODER_DEPTH + 2)`, which never reallocates while bounded, and a parking_lot Condvar in `Shared`. The jobs are:
   - `Frame { picture: CFRetained<CVPixelBuffer>, pts_us, keyframe, token }`. Cloning the picture is a CFRetain, not a pixel copy.
   - `Rate(u32)`
   - `Stop`

3. `Encoder::encode` still pushes `Pending` with `at = now` (462-468), so dwell and `late()` include any queue wait. It then pushes `Job::Frame`, notifies, and returns Ok(()). The `encode_frame` call and its error cleanup (472-494) move into the thread loop. On a non-zero status, the thread pops the matching Pending as 482-490 does, sets `state.failure` (the field the callback already uses, encoder.rs:62-63) and wakes thread C. `drain` (501-517) surfaces the failure through `codec_error`, so the H.265 EncoderFailed path is unchanged.

4. `set_bitrate` enqueues `Job::Rate`, so AverageBitRate and DataRateLimits are applied in frame order on the submit thread. It caches `self.bitrate` at once. An AverageBitRate refusal becomes `state.failure`.

5. `Drop` (520-526) enqueues Stop and joins with an OUTPUT_WAIT bound. The thread invalidates the session after its last call, so the callback refcon, which is the `Arc<Shared>` the thread holds, outlives every callback. On timeout the thread is detached; it owns its clones, so nothing dangles.

6. video.rs needs no logic change. `pending()` still counts queued Pending entries, so the ENCODER_DEPTH gate (video.rs:87) holds.

No per-frame allocation, spawn or copy is added: per frame there is one CFRetain and one condvar notify. The thread runs at default QoS: an A/B of user-interactive against default showed no dwell difference (4.9-6.1 ms for both).

Mechanism (measured): thread C stops blocking for 3-16 ms per frame in VideoToolbox at 16-aligned sizes and at 4K p95. The block drops to about 0.05 ms, one enqueue.

- synthetic per-frame clock: 32.5 to 33.6 dB.

critique.area: R2: macOS host VideoToolbox encoding. I reviewed it against crates/pb-mapper-desktop/src/platform/macos/{encoder.rs,video.rs,capture.rs}, worker/capture.rs, pacer.rs, qos.rs and codec/pipeline.rs at 1515eda, and against airhand 08e2db0. I re-measured with my own probe, which uses a ring of pre-painted surfaces and pb-mapper's pacing rules, so nothing is painted on the pacing thread (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lb7666--claude-spares-spare-vPIbq7/2de9709e-ea4b-442d-a692-7f9e8fd50cdd/scratchpad/notes/r2rev_queue.swift). I also re-ran the researcher's probe. Environment: Apple M6, macOS 27.0 (26A425), Swift 6.4.2 -O, load average 2-4 (one run at 17). Pictures are synthetic CVPixelBufferCreate NV12 IOSurfaces, not ScreenCaptureKit. Outputs are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lb7666--claude-spares-spare-vPIbq7/2de9709e-ea4b-442d-a692-7f9e8fd50cdd/scratchpad/notes/r2rev_*.txt.

reviews.factual_errors:
1. The 4K figure is wrong. With a caller that does no per-frame painting, 3840x2160 blocks for the whole encode at every pace: call p50 is 14.4-15.2 ms for both codecs at pace 30, 60 and 120 (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lb7666--claude-spares-spare-vPIbq7/2de9709e-ea4b-442d-a692-7f9e8fd50cdd/scratchpad/notes/r2rev_4k.txt and r2rev_queue_big.txt in the same directory). It is not "0.7 ms p50, 16.5 ms p95". 4K is the commonest case: a 4K, 5K or iMac display at the default Native limit.

2. The throughput claim is wrong ("1440p120 becomes practical"). pacer.rs consume(now) is called with the tick's start time (worker/capture.rs:333; `now` precedes the call), so a blocking call costs no throughput. Measured with pb-mapper's pacing: 2560x1440 at pace 120 gives 120.0 fps with a 7.4 ms blocking call, and 4K at pace 120 gives about 64-66 fps while blocking. The thread changes waiting on thread C (input, cursor sampling, control lane), not frame rate.

3. The evidence "182 of 240 at 4K in pb-mapper's own test" is not evidence about thread C. tests.rs Pacer::run paints every picture on the pacing thread (`paint(picture, self.frame)`), so it measures painting plus the call.

4. The proposed VecDeque job queue (capacity ENCODER_DEPTH+2) would queue pictures behind a synchronous encode, and VideoToolbox cannot overlap those. At synchronous sizes, throughput was identical at in-flight depths 4, 2 and 1: 2560x1440 at 120 fps, 3328x2160 at 75-80 fps. Every queued picture would wait a whole encode, up to 15 ms at 4K, for nothing, and would be staler than the one thread C would take after the wait.

5. Minor: the blocking also delays thread C's 16 ms cursor sampling and its control-lane commands.
reviews.effect_assessment:
The effect is real, and larger than claimed at 4K.

Call time measured here, synthetic surfaces, pb-mapper settings, low latency:
- Blocking sizes: 1920x1200 5.3-5.5 ms, 2560x1440 7.0-7.8 ms, 2560x1664 7.7-8.6 ms, 3008x1952 10.9 ms, 3328x2160 13.0 ms, 3840x2160 14.4-15.2 ms.
- 16-unaligned sizes return in 0.02-0.05 ms: 1920x1080, 1662x1080, 2228x1440, 3024x1964, 3340x2160.

Input arriving uniformly waits a mean of b²·fps/2, with p99 close to b. Estimated `input_wait` (enqueue to execution):

| Case | Mean | p99 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4K at 60 (thread C blocked 87% of the time) | ~6.3 ms | ~14 ms |
| 1440p at 60 | ~1.7 ms | ~7.3 ms |
| 1440p at 120 | ~3.3 ms | ~7.3 ms |
| 1920x1200 at 60 | ~0.9 ms | ~5.2 ms |

The documented gate (p99 ≤ 5 ms on the ordinary backend, docs/remote-desktop.md:1705-1708) fails at 1440p and 4K. The trait contract "Capture and submit one picture, without blocking" (platform/mod.rs, VideoSource::submit) and the worker.rs:1-5 claim are violated at those sizes.

After the change, encoding adds roughly nothing to `input_wait`, and cursor reports are no longer held up to 15 ms. Throughput and dwell are unchanged.

This applies whenever ScreenCaptureKit delivers a 16-aligned size, which is always the case for 4K, 5K, iMac and 1440p displays at Native or 1440p limits, and for more sizes if R2-vt-align-scaled-size lands. If ScreenCaptureKit's own buffers declare 16-padding (see R2-vt-align-scaled-size), every size blocks today, which makes this matter even more.

airhand does the same separation: a per-stream encoder thread (client/src-tauri/src/host/pipeline.rs:96-98) and a separate injector thread (host/input/thread.rs:82-96). Its synchronous encode_frame + complete_frames (encoder/vt.rs:416-445) never delays input.
reviews.corrected_design:
In platform/macos/encoder.rs:

1. Submitter and its one-slot mailbox
- Spawn one std::thread, "pb-mapper-vt-submit", in Encoder::build after prepare_to_encode_frames (encoder.rs:352-357). Do not spawn it for the encodes() probe (199-215).
- The thread owns a CFRetained<VTCompressionSession> clone, the prebuilt ForceKeyFrame dictionary and an Arc<Shared>. A SendSession newtype carries them, with a SAFETY note: CF objects are retained and released atomically, and every VideoToolbox call is serialised on this one thread. The pattern matches `unsafe impl Send for Picture` in capture.rs:72-73.
- Add a one-slot mailbox to Shared: `job: Option<Job>` and `rate: Option<u32>` under the existing state mutex, plus a parking_lot Condvar, `busy: bool` and `c_waiting: bool`. Job is `{ picture: CFRetained<CVPixelBuffer>, pts_us, keyframe, token }`: a CFRetain, no pixel copy and no per-frame allocation.
- Use no VecDeque of jobs.
- Wrap each job in objc2::rc::autoreleasepool. The thread has no pool otherwise; capture.rs brings its own for the same reason.

2. Encoder::encode (450-497)
- Compute pts and push Pending with at = now (462-468), exactly as today, so dwell, late() and the OUTPUT_WAIT stall check (506-515) are unchanged.
- Place the Job, set busy, notify and return Ok(()).
- The thread runs encode_frame and its error cleanup (472-494). On a non-zero status it pops the matching Pending, sets state.failure and wakes thread C. drain() surfaces the failure through codec_error, so H.265's EncoderFailed path is unchanged.
- After every call the thread clears busy. If c_waiting is set, it clears it and calls waker.wake().

3. Encoder::set_bitrate (410-431)
- Store `rate = Some(bitrate)` (latest wins), cache self.bitrate and notify.
- Before its next encode, or at once when idle, the thread applies AverageBitRate and DataRateLimits. An AverageBitRate refusal becomes state.failure.
- This removes the 0.17-2.6 ms property sets from thread C.

4. Add `Encoder::busy()`, which sets c_waiting when it returns true.

5. In video.rs MacVideo::submit (85-109), before taking a picture, when the encoder is busy, return Ok(false). Do not take the picture, and keep self.keyframe. The tick stays armed (worker/capture.rs:335-347), so the newest picture is taken the moment the encoder is free.
- Do not return Ok(true), which spends the tick. At 4K and pace 120, the tick grid would then cut throughput from today's ~66 fps (the overdue tick is taken as soon as the blocking call returns) to 60.

6. MacVideo::idle_until (110-120): while busy, return Some(Instant::now() + LATE_OUTPUT) instead of None.
- None means due now. For a push source (DRAIN None), capture_poll_after returns None, so None would make thread C spin. The real wake comes from the thread.

7. Drop (520-526)
- Put Stop in the mailbox, notify, and join with a LATE_OUTPUT bound. A synchronous encode is at most ~25 ms.
- The thread invalidates the session after its last call. If the join times out, the thread is detached; it owns its clones, so the refcon (Arc::as_ptr of Shared) stays valid until it exits.

8. Diagnostics (host log only): per second, the thread traces the VT call duration p50/p99 as `macos_encoder_call`. This confirms on a device which ScreenCaptureKit sizes are synchronous.

9. Docs and changelog
- The Mac paragraph in docs/remote-desktop.md, plus the worker.rs:1-5 comment and the VideoSource::submit comment if needed.
- The input_wait paragraph: state that on a Mac the encoder runs on its own submit thread.
- A CHANGELOG bullet.

- Dropping an Encoder mid-encode neither hangs nor calls back after Drop returns.

The effect is real but narrow.

In the 0.5-1.8 s after each IDR on links at ≤4 Mbit/s, about every other picture is dropped. IDRs follow a control grant or revoke, session start, resume and viewer requests. If the dropped picture is the last change (a typed character, the end of a scroll), the viewer keeps the previous picture until the 250 ms liveness repeat.

After the change it arrives one tick later (16.7 or 8.3 ms), up to ~230 ms sooner. The typical case is typing right after taking control on a constrained link.

missed.design:
The researcher dismissed padding because "it needs a capability-gated crop field implemented by all five viewers". It does not.
- H.264 and HEVC carry the visible size in the SPS (frame_cropping / conformance_window), and every viewer's decoder already honours it: every 1920x1080 or 1662x1080 stream VideoToolbox or Media Foundation produces today is coded padded and cropped by its SPS.
- kVTCompressionPropertyKey_CleanAperture does not write that crop. Tested here: the re-parsed SPS of a 1920x1088 or 3024x1968 session stays 1920x1088 or 3024x1968 with CleanAperture set (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lb7666--claude-spares-spare-vPIbq7/2de9709e-ea4b-442d-a692-7f9e8fd50cdd/scratchpad/notes/r2rev_clap.txt). So the host rewrites it.

Phase 0: the device diagnostic in R2-vt-align-scaled-size. Proceed only if ScreenCaptureKit's surfaces lack 16-padding.

Phase 1:

1. Sizes, in video.rs open: content = scaled_size(...) (exact, no rounding); coded = each dimension rounded up to a multiple of 16.

2. ScreenCaptureKit (capture.rs configuration): width and height = coded; destinationRect = (0, 0, content) (macOS 12.3+), so the display is written 1:1, or scaled as today, into the top-left. The remainder takes the configured black background.

3. Encoder: the VideoToolbox session is created at the coded size. VideoFormat.width/height report the content size, so the wire meaning is unchanged.

4. A new platform-neutral, pure codec/sps_crop.rs:
- RBSP unescape and re-escape, and an exp-Golomb reader and writer.
- H.264 SPS: parse through frame_mbs_only and direct_8x8, including the high-profile chroma, bit-depth and scaling-list fields. Then write frame_cropping_flag = 1 and the right and bottom offsets in CropUnit = 2 for 4:2:0 frame-only streams, and copy the remaining bits, VUI included.
- HEVC SPS: profile_tier_level with sub-layers, then chroma_format_idc and the picture size. Set conformance_window_flag and conf_win_right/bottom_offset in units of 2, and copy the rest.

5. Output path: in encoder.rs, rewrite the parameter sets once per CMFormatDescription, cached by its pointer, so only keyframes carry them and nothing is done per packet. They go to annex_b (encoder.rs:706-717).

6. Fallback: a parse failure at the first keyframe sets padding off for the process and fails the session once, and the rebuild uses today's exact size.

The same mechanism serves scaled sizes with exact aspect, and can replace the 16-rounding of R2-vt-align-scaled-size.

areas.name: Windows host capture and encoding after #62

research.area: R3: the Windows host after PR #62 (DXGI capture, video processor, Media Foundation encoder, helper pipe, thread C capture)
research.summary:
pb-mapper's Windows host captures on thread C, either in the app process or in the helper worker that privileged sharing ("Turn on remote control", ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop/host.rs:521-525) uses. Each submit calls AcquireNextFrame(0) (platform/windows/video/mod.rs:575), copies a new desktop into one full-resolution BGRA texture (611), and scales it with the D3D11 video processor (OPTIMAL_SPEED, converter.rs:53) into MF-allocated NV12 samples. These feed an async hardware MFT: low latency, CBR, QualityVsSpeed 0, infinite GOP, and H.264 Baseline or H.265 Main (codec.rs:202-237). Thread C polls that MFT's events every 2 ms (DRAIN_POLL, backend.rs:20; the Waker is ignored, platform/windows/mod.rs:125).

After E phase 1, an empty tick stays armed. Thread C polls every 2 ms for 250 ms after an input or a new picture, and once a period otherwise. The grid only moves later, and the present time is thrown away (video/mod.rs:581-584).

Through the helper, every capture, drain and pointer read is a synchronous request/reply. Each crosses two named pipes with 8 KiB quotas (pipe.rs:35-36), relayed by the service with 8 KiB copies (service.rs:237), and mio 1.2.4 reads them 4 KiB at a time. A drain long-poll of up to 4 ms blocks thread C and its input lane (worker/capture.rs:22,362-381). The worker answers with five desktop verifications per Video request.

airhand does several things differently:
- It blocks in AcquireNextFrame on its own capture thread.
- It stamps frames with LastPresentTime and paces on that timeline.
- It collects encoder output within 250 us.
- It encodes H.264 as High with CABAC.
- It refines a stopped picture with a short repeat burst.
- It handles rotated displays and FP16 (HDR) desktops.
- It has no privileged pipe.

pb-mapper is already ahead on:
- infinite GOP with read-back;
- encode-once fan-out to up to four viewers;
- IDR coalescing;
- a per-frame-budget QoS with its rate-model latch.

LowDelayVBR, LTR and raised CPU priority do not fit pb-mapper or were withdrawn.

candidates.title: Anchor capture pacing to DXGI's LastPresentTime (E phase 2) on the Windows host

- pace.rs:34-49 waits until next - period/4, then sets next = max(stamp, next - period/64) + period.
- capture/mod.rs:610-623 sleeps on that timeline and calls pacer.done(f.captured).
- Its tests (pace.rs:90-139) show that 60, 59.94 and 60.001 Hz sources are never delayed or skipped, and that 120-240 Hz sources are thinned to 58-62 fps.
candidates.pb_current:

- video/mod.rs:581-584 reads LastPresentTime only to detect novelty, then drops it. :529-530 stamps pts with the submit time.

candidates.title: Helper protocol 11: the worker pushes encoded units, fresh-picture notices and pointer updates; thread C stops long-polling the pipe
candidates.airhand_evidence:
airhand has no privileged pipe, and every hand-off in it is event-driven:
- the capture thread publishes into a FrameSlot, and the encoder thread blocks on its condvar (capture/mod.rs:378-407 wait_change; pipeline.rs:253-254);
- each unit is sent the moment it is encoded (pipeline.rs:404-449).

No stage polls another.
candidates.pb_current:
Host side:
- oop/client.rs:101-123: every backend call is a blocking write-then-read under block_on.
- client.rs:336-337: `bind` ignores the Waker. :341-343 drain_poll is 2 ms.
- worker/capture.rs:362-381: after each submit, thread C drains with a long-poll of up to HELPER_DRAIN_WAIT_MAX (4 ms, :22). Its input lane waits meanwhile.

Worker side:
- oop/server.rs:276-293 polls the encoder with sleep(1 ms).
- helper/worker.rs:114 sleeps on recv_timeout(15 ms).
- Every Video request reads the context and the pointer (server.rs:128, 232-242). Including capture_video's own checks (native.rs:188, 218, 257, 261), that is five desktop verifications per request.
- While hot, thread C makes such a round trip every 2 ms (worker/capture.rs:144-154).
- The pointer reaches the host only in answers (client.rs:259-268).
candidates.change:
Worker (platform/windows/helper/worker.rs:84-149):
- serve_bound waits on the crate's Waiter (platform/windows/waiter.rs), bound to the backend's Waker through PlatformBackend::bind, instead of recv_timeout.
- The exchange task (oop/server.rs:43-73) calls wake.notify() after each try_send.
- Each loop iteration serves pending requests first. Then, while the host has video on (a new Request::Stream{on, hot_ms}), it:
  - drains finished units and sends `Push::Unit{generation, video, pending}` plus the bytes record. This uses R3-mf-output-events; until that lands, a local 1 ms poll does.
  - sends `Push::Fresh{presented_ago_us}` when the source has a new picture. This uses R3-dxgi-present-waiter; until then, an AcquireNextFrame(0) on the worker's own thread every 2 ms while the host's hot window lasts. No verification is needed, since nothing is captured for the host yet.
  - reads the pointer every 16 ms and sends `Push::Pointer` only when it or the shape serial changed.
- exchange select!s between the next request and an mpsc of pushes, writing whole records in order.
- drain() (server.rs:276-293) is removed.

Host (oop/client.rs):
- connect_backend (helper/mod.rs:95-112) starts one I/O thread that owns the current_thread runtime and the NamedPipeClient.
- call() sends (Request, oneshot) to that thread and blocks for the reply.
- The I/O task demuxes:
  - Reply → the oneshot;
  - Unit → a bounded VecDeque (ENCODER_DEPTH + 2; overflow is a protocol error) plus Waker::wake;
  - Fresh → a flag plus wake;
  - Pointer → the cached cursor and serial.
- `bind` keeps the Waker. `drain_poll` → None.
- `drain_video` pops the queue with no pipe call and drops units of another generation.
- `pending_video` = the worker's pending + the queued units.
- `capture_idle_until` → None while a Fresh is pending or a keyframe is asked for; otherwise last_submit + LIVENESS_INTERVAL.
- Thread C then never long-polls this backend. HELPER_DRAIN_WAIT_MAX and DRAIN_WAIT_MAX_MS go.

Also:
- Bump HELPER_PROTOCOL and both pipe names.
- Update docs/remote-desktop.md (protocol paragraph), docs/architecture.md, and user-guide.md with user-guide.zh-CN.md, together.
candidates.expected_effect:
Estimates, unmeasured:
- Encoder output reaches thread C 0.5-1.3 ms sooner per frame. Today the first drain comes 2 ms after the submit, then the worker polls with 1 ms sleeps, which last 1-2 ms on Windows.
- Thread C no longer blocks its input lane for up to 4 ms in a drain long-poll every frame.
- Round trips while active drop from up to about 500/s (2 ms hot polls) to about one per new picture.
- Each round trip is estimated at 100-160 us of CPU across the host, the service relay and the worker's five desktop checks. That is about 4-6% of a core saved while the desktop moves.
- This applies to every privileged Windows session, the recommended setup.
candidates.risk:
- Reply and push interleaving must keep order. A bug there could deliver a unit after the context changed; generation tagging plus the host's check bound that.
- Pointer freshness has to come from pushes now that hot polls are gone.
- Background-service users must update the helper.
- The named-pipe I/O thread and the worker loop compile only on the Windows CI runner.

- The output size comes from the rotated dimensions: scaled_size (297-300) takes (height, width) for 90 and 270.

converter.rs, Converter::new:
- Takes the rotation.
- Checks the rotation cap through GetVideoProcessorCaps.
- Calls VideoProcessorSetStreamRotation(processor, 0, true, ROTATION_90/180/270).
- The content description's input stays the unrotated texture, and so does the source rect (68-78). The dest rect is the rotated output.
- Without the cap, today's error stays.

Input needs no change: the Display geometry and input mapping already use the rotated orientation (desktop.rs:92-108, GetMonitorInfoW).
candidates.protocol: None. The video simply has the rotated size, which matches the Display already sent.
candidates.expected_effect: A rotated (portrait) display can be shared. Today every attempt fails.
candidates.measure:
On a Windows device:
- Rotate a monitor to each of 90, 180 and 270 degrees.
- Run `video_bench 10 60 --animate` on it and a real session.
- Check that the picture is upright, that a click lands where aimed, and the VP Blt time, against an unrotated run.

- A GPU whose video processor lacks rotation keeps failing as today.
- Each orientation must be checked on a device.

candidates.title: Move helper units in large pipe reads: mio 1.2.5, larger pipe quotas and relay buffers, one write per record
candidates.airhand_evidence: none
candidates.pb_current:
- Cargo.lock pins mio 1.2.4. Its named-pipe reads are always 4 KiB (mio-1.2.4 src/sys/windows/named_pipe.rs:726-729, 827-829).
- pipe.rs:35-36 sets 8 KiB in and out quotas.
- service.rs:237 relays with tokio::io::copy_bidirectional, which uses 8 KiB buffers (tokio io/util/mod.rs:88).
- ipc.rs:20-31 writes the length, then the body, then flushes. With mio, each write waits for the previous overlapped completion, so a reply plus its image costs 4 sequential completions.
- A 170 KB 1080p IDR crosses each of the two hops in about 43 reads. A 4K IDR of up to 3.7 MB takes about 900.
candidates.change:
1. `cargo update -p mio --precise 1.2.5`, a lockfile change only. mio 1.2.5 sizes each read to the caller's buffer, from 4 KiB up to 64 KiB (named_pipe.rs:280-290, 805-821).
2. pipe.rs:35-36: in and out buffer size of 1 MiB. This is a quota, bounded by ipc::MAX_FRAME.
3. service.rs:237: `tokio::io::copy_bidirectional_with_sizes(&mut caller, &mut private, 256 * 1024, 256 * 1024)`, available in tokio 1.49 (copy_bidirectional.rs:94).
4. ipc.rs: write_bytes builds `len | bytes` into one buffer and makes one write_all. server.rs:62-65 and client.rs:110-112 send the JSON record and the image record as one buffer.

The framing stays byte-identical.
candidates.protocol: None. The records on the pipe are byte-identical; only how they are written and read changes.
candidates.expected_effect:
Estimates:
- A 170 KB IDR needs about 3 reads per hop instead of about 43; 20-50 KB P-frames need 1 instead of 5-13; each call needs 1 write completion instead of 2-4.
- Per IDR that saves an estimated 0.5-1 ms at 1080p, several ms at 4K, and roughly 10-20 ms for the largest units.
- The service relay and the worker spend fewer CPU wakes on 4K Quality sessions.
candidates.measure:
On a Windows device:
- Write a micro-bench in examples/ that sends 20 KB, 170 KB, 1 MB and 3.7 MB records through a service-style relay of two named pipes. Report time per record and IOCP completions, at mio 1.2.4 and 1.2.5, release builds.
- Measure the worker-to-host unit delay of real IDRs through the helper.

On the Mac: `cargo test --workspace` after the mio bump.
candidates.risk:
- A mio patch release changes every platform's I/O. CI's NAT traversal and the workspace tests cover it.
- A 1 MiB pipe quota is nonpaged pool per pipe: two pipes per session, at most 8 instances.

candidates.title: Convert straight from the duplication surface and keep an encoded-size NV12 copy for repeats, instead of a full-resolution BGRA copy per new picture
candidates.airhand_evidence: none. airhand copies into its own pool texture (capture/dxgi.rs:534-558) because several sessions share one capture. Only its immediate Flush after the copy (555-556) is adopted.
candidates.pb_current:
- video/mod.rs:586-611 copies every new desktop image into `latest` with a full-resolution BGRA CopyResource (8 bytes/px of traffic). Only then does the video processor read `latest` again (520-528).
- Repeats and keyframes on a still desktop re-run the video processor from `latest`.
- AllocateSample runs after acquire (523-527), so an empty pool still consumes the new picture's tick.
candidates.change:
video/mod.rs, submit:
- Allocate the sample first. MF_E_SAMPLEALLOCATOR_EMPTY → Full before anything is acquired.
- On a new present:
  - Blt from the acquired DXGI texture straight into the sample. Converter::convert caches the input view per texture pointer, and DXGI usually returns one surface.
  - CopySubresourceRegion the NV12 sample into a `last_nv12` texture of the encoded size (1.5 bytes/px).
  - Flush, then ReleaseFrame.
- For a liveness repeat or keyframe on a still desktop, copy `last_nv12` into a fresh sample; no video processor and no BGRA texture.
- Drop `latest`. Keep the 'first frame' rule of R3-first-frame.
- GPU work queued before ReleaseFrame is ordered before DWM's next write, as with today's CopyResource.

If R3-dxgi-present-waiter lands, the same conversion moves into its thread, and this candidate is folded into it.
candidates.protocol: None.
candidates.expected_effect:
Per new picture, estimated from bytes moved:
- 4K captured, 1080p encoded: about 102 MB → 42 MB.
- 1440p native: 50 MB → 31 MB.
- 4K native: 112 MB → 70 MB.

That is about 0.1-0.2 ms on a discrete GPU, and about 0.5-1 ms plus less memory-bandwidth contention on an iGPU. Static repeats skip the video processor entirely.
candidates.risk:
- Some driver might refuse a video processor input view on the duplication surface. Fall back to today's copy when CreateVideoProcessorInputView fails.
- The MF allocator may hand out texture-array subresources (converter.rs:191-201); the copy must address the subresource.

candidates.title: Raise the GPU scheduling priority of the capture device while a session streams
candidates.airhand_evidence: none
candidates.pb_current:
- video/mod.rs:301-302 and 639-657 use the duplication device at default GPU priority.
- Under a GPU-bound foreground app (a game, a 3D tool), the host's CopyResource, VideoProcessorBlt and encoder input queue behind that app's command buffers.
- F, CPU thread priority, was a different item, measured only on the Mac.
candidates.change:
In platform/windows, a guard held while at least one session streams, like TimerResolution::hold (timer.rs):
- In build() (249-369), call `device.cast::<IDXGIDevice>()?.SetGPUThreadPriority(7)`. It needs SeIncreaseBasePriorityPrivilege, which the SYSTEM helper worker has; the unelevated app fails harmlessly.
- Call D3DKMTSetProcessSchedulingPriorityClass(GetCurrentProcess(), D3DKMT_SCHEDULINGPRIORITYCLASS_HIGH) through the windows Wdk_Graphics_Direct3D feature or GetProcAddress on gdi32. Read the old class first and restore it when the last session stops. Never use REALTIME, which can starve DWM.
- Log success or failure once.
candidates.protocol: None.
candidates.expected_effect:
Estimated:
- While another app saturates the GPU, capture-to-encoder-output stops waiting behind that app's frames. Sunshine, which does this, cites removed stutter at 100% GPU.
- No effect on an idle GPU.
candidates.risk:
- HIGH class can slow the foreground game slightly.
- Behaviour differs with hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling.
- The in-process app usually lacks the privilege for the thread priority, so most of the gain comes through the helper.

candidates.title: Capture FP16 (HDR) desktops and tone-map them to SDR on the GPU
candidates.airhand_evidence:
- client/src-tauri/src/host/capture/dxgi.rs:390-391 lists BGRA8 and R16G16B16A16_FLOAT.
- dxgi.rs:474-497 duplicates with DuplicateOutput1 using that list.
- capture/dxgi/hdr.rs:20-50 converts FP16 frames with a shader. The shader (hdr.hlsl) scales by the display's SDR white level (hdr.rs:56-90, DisplayConfigGetDeviceInfo) and rolls highlights off.

candidates.pb_current:
- video/mod.rs:280-281 duplicates with BGRA8 only. On an HDR desktop, DXGI converts the FP16 desktop itself, without the display's SDR white level, so SDR content arrives at the wrong brightness.

candidates.change:
video/mod.rs:
- Ask for [R16G16B16A16_FLOAT, BGRA8]: add an FP16 entry to windows-capture's DxgiDuplicationFormat list, or call IDXGIOutput5::DuplicateOutput1 directly if it has none.
- For an FP16 frame, draw a full-screen triangle that reads the duplication texture through an SRV, scales by 1/(SDR white / 80 nits), rolls highlights off and encodes sRGB, into the BGRA render target (`latest`, which already has BIND_RENDER_TARGET at 594). The video processor runs as today.

candidates.protocol: None.
candidates.expected_effect: Users with HDR turned on see the shared desktop at the same SDR brightness and color as locally. Today DXGI's own conversion misjudges it. The cost is one full-screen shader pass per new picture, only on HDR desktops.
candidates.measure:
On a Windows device with HDR on:
- Show a known SDR test pattern at several SDR-content-brightness settings.
- Compare a `video_bench --output` dump decoded with ffmpeg against the pattern (PSNR, mean luma), before and after.
- Measure the pass's GPU time with D3D11 timestamp queries.
candidates.risk:
- The DXGI fallback conversion differs by driver, so the before-state must be recorded on a device.
- Wide-gamut content is clipped to sRGB primaries.

candidates.protocol: None.
candidates.expected_effect: A host whose desktop is completely still when a session or an encoder rebuild starts shows its picture at once. The rebuilds come after a display change, a desktop switch or a recovery. Today such a desktop may show nothing for 3 s and then fail until the screen changes. The probability depends on the driver and is unmeasured.

On a Windows device:

candidates.title: Encode AV1 with the GPU's Media Foundation encoder when the viewer lists an av1 capability (G, host side)
candidates.airhand_evidence:
- client/src-tauri/src/host/encoder/mf.rs:29-35 maps Codec::AV1 to MFVideoFormat_AV1.
- mf.rs:907-913 detects AV1 keyframes by CleanPoint.
- mf.rs:919-920 relies on the sequence header OBU in keyframes.

candidates.pb_current:
- codec.rs:480-485 knows only H.264 and HEVC subtypes.
- VideoCodec has no AV1.
- The negotiation pattern exists for H.265: the viewer capability `h265` (protocol.rs:26), Accepted{codec}, the probe (video/probe.rs), and the H265_FAILED latch (worker.rs:63).

candidates.change:
Host side, this area:
- VideoCodec::Av1, negotiated only when the viewer lists `av1`. Rank AV1 > H.265 > H.264 when the backend encodes it.
- codec.rs: subtype MFVideoFormat_AV1. No profile property (Main). Low latency and CBR as today. GOP set and read back. The B-frame property is checked as for H.265.
- A neutral OBU parser in src/codec/:
  - a temporal unit is a keyframe when its frame header has frame_type KEY_FRAME and show_frame;
  - prepend the last sequence header OBU when a keyframe lacks it;

- The helper's Request::H265 generalises to Request::Encodes{codec} (protocol bump, shared with R3-helper-push).

The viewer decoders belong to the viewer areas:
- Windows: the AV1 Video Extension MFT.
- macOS: VideoToolbox AV1 on M3 and later.
- Linux: GStreamer.
- Android: MediaCodec.
- The FFI's DecoderOffer.
candidates.expected_effect:
Unmeasured on pb-mapper:
- A sharper picture at the same bits per frame where both ends have AV1 hardware: RTX 40/50, Intel Arc or Core Ultra, AMD RDNA3 hosts.
- It widens reach for Windows-to-Windows pairs whose viewer lacks the paid HEVC extension but decodes AV1. Those sessions run H.264 today.

candidates.measure:
On a Windows device: `video_bench 20 60 --pace 60,30,15,5 --codec av1|h265|h264` at equal bits per frame. Compare mean QP or PSNR on `--output` dumps decoded by ffmpeg, keyframe counts and dwell.

End to end: a Windows AV1 host with Windows and M-series Mac viewers.

- Large cross-area change: wire capability, helper bump, a decoder on every viewer.
- Each vendor's AV1 MFT behaviour (GOP, rate model, sequence headers) is unknown until measured.
- Every encoder line goes unexecuted in CI.

On a Windows device:
