prs.name: receipt-rate-control
prs.title: Receipt-driven rate control (D stage 1): cut bits per frame within a round trip, keep the frame rate, and cut fps only from the delivery rate at the preset floor
prs.protocol_changes: None (wire, helper pipe and FFI unchanged; VideoRate already travels with each capture call).
prs.design:
Why. Receipts feed only send credit; frame rate and bits per frame follow the 1/s or 4/s probe, fps by RustDesk delay steps and bpf every 3 s in 5-20% steps (qos.rs:600-661, 664-731). Congestion therefore costs frame rate first: the recorded 1 Mbit/s case ends at pace 10 while bpf hardly moves (docs/benchmarks/2026-11-24-desktop-pipeline/slow_link.txt). Stage 0 already ships the shadow estimator (qos/receipt_rate.rs: standing_ms, busy_bps, would_cut) and Receipt {delay, bytes, behind_idr} from credit.rs. airhand does all rate control on per-frame acks (crates/airhand-link/src/flow.rs:555-616, cut min(0.85 x busy, 0.9 x estimate), episodes and rebase, raise 15%/s or 4%/s near capacity).

Build stage 1 of the D design (scratchpad research D-fast-rate-control), adapted:
1. receipt_rate.rs acts: on_sample returns a Verdict {None | Hold | Cut(target_bps) | Rebased}: raw = delay - base minus the frame allowance (min(frame interval, bytes x 8 / busy)); rebase tracked as a minimum (receipt-local, the probe base untouched); standing = min of the last 3 queues, before = min of the 3 before; skip samples behind an IDR; busy = median per-pair rate over the last 8 pairs where the link stayed busy (None below 3); congested = standing > QUEUE_HIGH (40 ms) || (blocked && standing > QUEUE_LOW (10 ms)), with `blocked` counted only while the window is clamped. Congested: inside a hold nothing; draining (standing + 5 ms < before, or < 0.8 x the episode's last) -> Hold; two cuts that left it within 1.1x -> Rebased; no busy rate -> None (no blind cut, the probe controller remains). Stage 0's stall and burst rule stays as it is.
2. Cut and hold (R8 (g)): hold until both max(rtt + standing, 100 ms) has passed and used <= 1.1 x target, for at most 1 s. Cut to min(0.85 x busy, 0.9 x used), or 0.85 x used when stalls recur. Remember capacity = busy.
3. qos.rs cut_to(target): p = pace, floor = preset floor x pixel scale; if target/p >= floor: bpf = min(bpf, target/p), adaptation LoweringBitrate; else bpf = floor and rate_fps = Some((target/floor).max(min_fps).min(p)), adaptation LoweringFps. pace() adds .min(rate_fps) before the startup, unresponsive and JPEG clamps. One owner for `adaptation`; Quality keeps its order: bpf to bpf_start/2, then fps from the delivery rate, then bpf to the floor.
4. Raise on the 250 ms tick when samples are fresh, no hold or episode, standing < QUEUE_LOW, rebase not growing and used >= 0.5 x expected: credit += per_s x dt (dt <= 500 ms; 0.04 near capacity (>= 0.9x), else 0.15) plus 100 kbit/s per second; apply at >= 5%; clear capacity above 1.2x. With rate_fps set, lift the fps cap first. Recovery accelerator, required (R8 (b)): when an episode has ended and standing has stayed under 10 ms for >= 500 ms, raise at 50%/s toward 0.9 x the expected rate held when the episode began, once per episode, skipping the 4%/s band; if that climb is cut below 0.9 x that rate, fall back to 15%/s and 4%/s.
5. Ownership and baseline (R8 (a)): control_fps yields to receipts only while an episode is active or within 2 s of a receipt cut or rebase (no 'standing < 40 ms' term); in the >= CUT_DELAY branch an owned arm holds fps below SEVERE_DELAY (600 ms); without ownership, or at >= 600 ms, today's arms run unchanged. On Rebased record rebase_offset = own_min - probe_base capped at CUT_DELAY (150 ms); control_fps computes delay against probe_base + rebase_offset; clear the offset when the 60 s probe base itself rises past it and on Path, resume, set_preset and reset_baseline, so both controllers share one baseline and queue creep is bounded by 150 ms plus the probe steps.
6. One-way inputs (R8 (d)): when arrival_time is negotiated (viewer-feedback), standing and busy come from the forward queue and viewer-clock spacing; otherwise from RTT receipts with stage 0's allowance.
7. Balanced H.264/H.265 starts at its ceiling whatever the first probe's RTT: remove the FAST_START_RTT gate at qos.rs:503-505 (receipts now cut within a round trip) (R8 (e)).
8. close_window: the rate-model latch is unchanged (rate-model-latch made it per tick, so mid-window cuts never latch Timestamp); step_bpf is skipped when receipts produced samples since the window started; JPEG and windows without receipts keep today's step.
9. Resets: set_preset -> fast.reset() and rate_fps = None; resume -> restart (samples, episode, hold); reset_baseline -> reset including rebase, capacity and rebase_offset.
10. session.rs and sender.rs: Session gains `blocked: AtomicBool`; admissible() reads qos.clamp_rate(now) and passes it to credit.window (credit.window gains `clamp: Option<u64>`: during an episode bytes = (DELIVERY_FACTOR x rate x t / 8).clamp(BYTE_WINDOW_CLAMP_MIN, normal), applied immediately); when fits is false and no IDR is in flight, under the same credit lock, store blocked = true; handle Received swaps it into qos.on_receipt; lock order unchanged (no credit and qos nesting). The feedback trace gains bpf, rate_fps, standing_ms, busy_bps, rebase_ms, cuts.
11. Mac hosts shed bandwidth with the fps part only with the Timestamp start (mac-vt-rate-control); VideoToolbox's response to a cut is measured and handled there (R8 (f)).
12. Decision record: DECISIONS D5 and CONTRACT-perf R13 (docs/remote-desktop-overhaul/plan/DECISIONS.md) say the probe owns fps and bitrate with receipts only clamping the byte window; record this deviation and the user's directive explicitly, as DECISIONS.md:1-5 requires.
13. Docs: QoS, send credit, constants; benchmark record indexed in docs/README.md; CHANGELOG bullet saying the rate target changes within a round trip, with measured figures only.

prs.name: reconnect-start-rate
prs.title: Start a reconnecting viewer's session at the rate the previous session ended at
prs.protocol_changes: None.
prs.design:
Why. Reconnects happen most on slow links, yet each new session starts at the preset's bpf_start: Balanced's first 1080p IDR is about 267 kbit at bpf_start against about 67 kbit at the floor (Quality about 800 against 200), and the startup pace of 30 x bpf_start is 2 Mbit/s on a 1 Mbit/s link, a queue bounded only by the 2x window (about 0.5 s of data at a 36 ms base). Estimate: the first picture after a reconnect on 1 Mbit/s arrives about 0.2-0.6 s sooner.

1. The host Room (host.rs) keeps one record: the bpf of the last session that ended by transport loss (End::Closed or HOST_READ_TIMEOUT), relative to 1080p, its preset, and when it ended.
2. A session accepted within 2 min with the same preset starts with bpf = min(the preset's start, the remembered bpf, rescaled to its picture). Qos::new takes an optional start (session.rs:198 passes it). Balanced's fps fast start is unchanged. A record older than 2 min, or from another preset, is ignored; the record only ever lowers the start.
3. A different viewer on a fast link within 2 min starts lower and climbs at the receipt controller's rate (receipt-rate-control's accelerator).
4. Docs: QoS startup paragraph; CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.name: encoder-throughput-cap
prs.title: Cap the pace at the encoder's measured throughput when units queue four deep, so dwell falls back to one or two service times
prs.protocol_changes: None. The pace Stats already report reflects the cap. No helper field (see design).
prs.design:
Why. When a Media Foundation encoder is slower than the pace and serial at its bottleneck while still accepting input, four units queue and each waits behind three: an 11 ms encoder at pace 120 has about 44 ms dwell, uneven. Capping the pace at what it delivers gives 11-16 ms with even spacing. NVIDIA is unaffected (3.1 ms at 4K); AMD and Intel at 4K or 1440p 120 are unmeasured, so how often this triggers is shown by its trace. Mac hosts are covered by their submit thread's two-in-flight gate and the H.265 standard-RC switch.

Simplified from the proposal: no Backend::encoder_full and no helper `full` field. After win-mf-output-events, Submit::Full means only MAX_IN_FLIGHT (= ENCODER_DEPTH, which thread C already sees as pending_video() >= ENCODER_DEPTH) or a rare empty sample allocator; the serial-before-NeedInput case is Submit::Waiting, which keeps the tick armed and builds no queue.
1. worker/window.rs counts full ticks per second (ticks where pending_video() >= ENCODER_DEPTH), apart from transport skips, with units produced and dwell p50.
2. Rule: full ticks >= max(2, pace/10) in a second set cap = max(the preset's min_fps, floor(0.95 x units)); after 3 s without a full tick the cap rises by max(1, cap/20); it clears at the QoS pace.
3. Apply it in capture_step's min pace (worker/capture.rs) and publish it as an AtomicU32 in each slot's SessionShared (shared.rs) that the session hands to its Qos (session.rs), whose pace() takes min with it (qos.rs, like viewer_cap at qos.rs:590-597).
4. Pipelined guard: keep the dwell p50 of the second before capping; if 2 s after capping dwell p50 is not below 0.6x of it, lift the cap and do not cap again for 30 s (latency, not throughput, filled the queue).
5. Trace `desktop_encoder_cap` {cap, full_ticks, units, dwell_before, dwell_after}.
6. Docs: the pacing paragraph and Diagnostics; CHANGELOG bullet only with device evidence of a vendor that triggers it.
prs.verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`: worker tests: a serial Fake at 11 ms per unit at pace 120 settles near 86 with pending <= 2 and dwell <= 2 service times; a pipelined Fake with 45 ms latency at pace 120 (full at depth 4) is capped, then lifted within 2 s, and does not ratchet; the cap rises back when the serial Fake speeds up. `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. prs.name: viewer-fps-cap
prs.title: Viewer: remember the decoder's capacity in the fps cap, raise in steps scaled to the ceiling, and drain an age backlog instead of freezing until the IDR
prs.protocol_changes: None (no protocol, FFI or runner change; fixed rings, no allocation per unit).
prs.design:
Why. (a) A consumer slower than the host (Linux software decode, Windows software MF in VMs, 4K120 on weak iGPUs) overshoots about every 5-6 s; most overshoots end in an age drop, a frozen picture until an IDR arrives and an IDR bandwidth spike; slow_presenter's mean pace is 12.4 for a 14.9 fps consumer. (b) At a 120 ceiling a transient backlog that halves the cap to 60 takes about 14 s to clear (CAP_STEP 5 per second after a 3 s hold). (c) On an age backlog the sink drops the queue at push (sink.rs:399-402) and take (599-601) as soon as the head is 250 ms old with 3 queued, sets wait_key and discards every later P-frame, so a consumer whose thread stalled 300 ms then returned shows nothing until the IDR (250 ms + RTT + encode + IDR transfer, over a second on 1 Mbit/s). airhand drains moderate backlogs and resets only beyond 8 queued in the decoder or 120 frames (client/src/lib/video.ts:34-35, 108-112, 171); its cap probes 15%/s far from capacity and 4%/s near it.

All in viewer/sink.rs and viewer/fps_cap.rs:
1. Signals per 250 ms tick: pulls (units take() handed out); backlogged tick (queue non-empty at both ends, no restart or drop between); measured capacity = pulls in backlogged ticks over their time across the last 8 ticks, valid once >= 4 backlogged ticks (1 s); head wait (age of the queue head); consumer lag: record presented_at - handed_at (sink.rs:704-741) in a 128-slot ring, excess = median over the last 1 s minus minimum over the last 10 s (near 0 on Darwin and Windows; grows by a decode time per hidden unit on a saturated Linux pipeline).
2. Lowering: today's triggers (a drop or backlog episode, or more than 2 queued on two ticks) plus excess consumer lag over max(2/cap s, 40 ms) on two ticks. capacity = the measured capacity when valid, else presented_fps; cap = floor(capacity x 0.9 direct or 0.8 relayed), at least CAP_MIN; the halving bound applies only when capacity came from presented_fps. Remember capacity and when.
3. Raising: with no known capacity, or up to hold = floor(0.95 x capacity): 3 s hold then one change a second, step = max(CAP_STEP x max(1, round(ceiling / 30)), ceil(0.25 x cap)) (R10's ceiling scaling: 20 at 120, 10 at 60, 5 at 30, merged with R5's 25% step). Above hold a raise is a probe: step max(1, ceil(0.1 x capacity)), allowed only after probe_backoff since the last failed probe (3 s doubling to 60 s, reset by a successful probe).
4. Probe watch (3 s after a probe): one tick with (>= 2 queued and head wait > max(2/cap s, 40 ms)) or excess consumer lag above the same reverts at once to the pre-probe cap (exempt from CAP_CHANGE_MIN) and doubles probe_backoff; a probe that survives forgets capacity and resets the backoff.
5. Forget capacity on a new generation, a picture-size change or a preset change.
6. Age backlog drains (R5-drain-age-backlog): on age, at push or take, when no age episode is open: open one, request the IDR through Recovery as today (KeyframeReason::Backlog; limiter and backoff unchanged, so the request time is unchanged), count it in backlog_drops (its meaning becomes 'backlog episodes'), tell the fps cap once, and do NOT clear the queue or set wait_key; keep enqueueing. The episode closes when an IDR is pushed (which already supersedes the queue with discontinuity, sink.rs:377-394) or the head's age falls below BACKLOG_AGE/2. Overflow (32 units, 8 MiB) still drops to the next IDR exactly as today. Recovery is unchanged (the awaited-IDR episode ends only when the IDR or a later frame is presented); the stall watchdog is unchanged.
7. Unchanged: CAP_MIN, the factors, the ceiling and its removal (sending max_fps), freeze() and the 500 ms IDR_GRACE judging.
8. Docs: 'Viewer: newest decodable frame, fps cap and recovery' and the sink module doc; CHANGELOG bullet with measured figures.

prs.name: mac-viewer-layer
prs.title: macOS viewer: present each decoded 420v picture on a native Core Animation layer from the decoder thread, skipping VideoToolbox's BGRA pass and Flutter's frame
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire, capabilities, helper or FFI; receipts still go through pb_mapper_desktop_video_presented_v1. App-internal pb_mapper/desktop_video channel only: a 'presenter' argument on create, a 'grey' method, a platform view type 'pb_mapper/desktop_video_view', and timings.present in stats.
prs.design:
Why. Today the Mac viewer decodes to BGRA (VideoToolbox's conversion pass: 33 MB written per 4K frame) and hands a CVPixelBuffer to a Flutter texture, so each picture waits for Flutter's next frame on the merged platform/UI thread, then raster and composite. Measured here (paced 60 fps): decode 0.7-1.3 ms less per frame at 1080p and 3-4 ms less at 4K with 420v; the first picture after stillness 3-6 ms sooner at 4K (scratchpad notes R6-macos-viewer-measurements.txt, r6rev_vt*.swift). Estimated from the Flutter source: about one refresh less from decode to glass (12-16 ms at 60 Hz, 6-8 at 120, 5-7 at 144), no jitter from a busy UI thread, lower power, and video that keeps moving during a live window resize. airhand presents on decode off the UI thread.

Scope: macOS only (#if os(macOS)); iOS and a macOS escape hatch (--dart-define=presenter=texture) keep the texture path; the presenter is chosen per viewer at create.
Swift (ui/darwin/DesktopVideo.swift):
1. create takes presenter: 'layer'|'texture' and still replies with an Int id; in layer mode the id comes from the plugin's own counter with no FlutterTexture registration; the texture limit and instance check are unchanged.
2. In layer mode VideoDecoder.attributes asks for kCVPixelFormatType_420YpCbCr8BiPlanarVideoRange with IOSurface properties and Metal compatibility (kept for mac-viewer-enhance).
3. Colour: in layer mode, after describe(), always rebuild the format description with TransferFunction = kCMFormatDescriptionTransferFunction_sRGB (10.13+; the app targets 10.15), primaries 709 and the stream's matrix (709 when absent), regardless of withBt709's early return and the VUI. At configure check the first decoded buffer carries the sRGB transfer attachment; if VideoToolbox did not carry it, set it per picture with CVBufferSetAttachment(.shouldPropagate) before the commit.
4. LayerPresenter, created at create (commits can precede the view): a container CALayer and a content CALayer (isOpaque, contentsGravity .resize, linear filters, autoresizing width and height). present(picture) on the feed thread: CATransaction.begin(); setDisableActions(true); content.contents = CVPixelBufferGetIOSurface(buffer); CATransaction.commit(). Keep the last three CVPixelBuffers referenced and set `shown`. Then copyPixelBuffer's receipt logic: under the lock the revision check, presented += 1, timings.present from decode end to commit end; after the commit, outside the lock, library.presented. publish() calls the presenter instead of hopping to main. No layer property is touched on that thread outside an explicit transaction, no NSView there.
5. DesktopVideoView: NSView, layer-hosting (layer = container before wantsLayer = true); default hitTest; acceptsFirstMouse true; acceptsFirstResponder false (keys stay with FlutterView); no mouse, scroll or magnify overrides (NSResponder forwards to FlutterView); layerContentsRedrawPolicy .never; layerUsesCoreImageFilters true. Cursor: resetCursorRects adds none; a tracking area [.cursorUpdate, .inVisibleRect, .activeAlways] whose cursorUpdate(with:) leaves the current cursor (no super call); if a check still shows the arrow, re-set NSCursor.current there.
6. View factory: DesktopVideoPlugin conforms to FlutterPlatformViewFactory (createArgsCodec FlutterStandardMessageCodec), registered with registrar.register(self, withId: 'pb_mapper/desktop_video_view') in register(); create(withViewIdentifier:arguments:) hosts that viewer's container layer; if Flutter recreates the view, the container moves on the main thread.
7. grey {textureId, on} on the main thread: content.filters = [CIColorMatrix with GreyStill's coefficients (viewer_overlays.dart:395-400)] or nil.
8. While attached and not paused, on macOS 14+, an NSView.displayLink asks preferredFrameRateRange up to the screen's maximum; its callback only counts, while stats timings are on, commits beyond the first in each refresh as `dropped`; before 14 a CVDisplayLink for that counting only. Keep the frame-rate request only if the ProMotion device check shows it is needed.
9. Snapshot keeps using `shown`; VTCreateCGImageFromCVPixelBuffer takes 420v.
Dart:
10. desktop_video.dart sends presenter: 'layer' on macOS unless --dart-define=presenter=texture; DesktopVideoTexture gains `String? platformViewType` (null in texture mode) and `Future<void> grey(bool on)`; FakeDesktopApi's texture returns null and a no-op.
11. viewer_stage.dart:186-196: with a platformViewType build AppKitView(key: ValueKey(id), viewType, creationParams {'textureId': id}, StandardMessageCodec, hitTestBehavior opaque), otherwise the Texture.
12. GreyStill (viewer_overlays.dart) calls texture.grey(on) when the texture has a native presenter (BackdropFilter cannot reach native content); linux-video-plane reuses this.
13. Docs: 'The app's video path' (remote-desktop.md:1990-1996) and 'macOS, iOS and Linux decoders' (2215-2227): the receipt now means committed to the WindowServer; the quality panel's Mac row; CHANGELOG bullet.

(b) Colour: build a pb-mapper-like stream (NV12 from sRGB values with the 709 matrix, no transfer conversion, VUI 709 as encoder.rs:338-351), decode to 420v with the forced sRGB tag and render with CARenderer against VT-BGRA (within 2 levels on 8 patches); then on screen, a known-pattern clip through desktop_ui_host screenshotted with Screenshot.app for both presenters. prs.name: viewer-refresh
prs.title: Desktop viewers: follow the refresh rate of the display the window is on, exactly (59.94, 119.88 on Windows), with the existing FpsCap message
prs.protocol_changes: No wire or capability change: reuses ViewerMessage::FpsCap (protocol.rs:188-191), which every peer accepts, and limits.max_fps at connect. FFI: one new op `{"op":"display_refresh","hz":<f64>}` of the existing pb_mapper_desktop_viewer_call_json export, changed on every side at once (Rust export, Dart DesktopApi interface, implementation, FakeDesktopApi). Windows runner: a `refresh_hz` method on the app's own pb_mapper/desktop_video channel.
prs.design:
Why. (a) The viewer asks for its display's refresh only at connect (and on macOS the fastest screen), so a Smooth session whose window moves from a 120 Hz to a 60 Hz screen keeps encoding, sending and decoding 120 fps of which half are superseded, at half the bits per frame; moving back does not resume 120 without a reconnect. (b) Windows viewers on 1000/1001 modes (59.94, 119.88 Hz: TVs, HDMI timings, some panels) ask 59 or 119 because Flutter reports whole hertz, so a 60/120 Hz host loses about one present a second while content moves: a hitch every second.

Rust (viewer/fps_cap.rs, sink.rs, mod.rs):
1. FpsCap gains `display_fps: Option<u32>` and `display_changed: bool`, set through set_display(fps). ceiling = if fps_override { max_fps } else { min(ceiling_fps(preset), max_fps, display_fps) } (a user-chosen rate ignores the display: the frames are fresher).
2. `release` = display_fps.filter(|d| !fps_override && *d < max_fps).unwrap_or(max_fps): the value meaning 'no backlog cap'. Every place that sends max_fps today sends release instead, including the raise-to-ceiling branch, so a backlog recovery never clears the display limit.
3. On display_changed the next tick sends the new effective value at once, bypassing CAP_CHANGE_MIN, the high-tick gate and the 3 s raise hold: min(backlog cap, display) when lowering, release when no backlog cap; while frozen (paused) it applies at the first tick after resume. Backlog lowering (viewer-fps-cap's capacity logic) keeps working beneath the display ceiling.
4. sink.rs set_display_fps; Viewer::set_display_refresh(hz: f64) rounds and clamps to MIN_VIEWER_FPS..=MAX_FPS as VideoLimits::choose does (Android ignores it, as choose does); session.rs:583-585 already forwards what tick returns. video.rs: a unit test pins 59.94 -> 60 and 119.88 -> 120.
FFI and Dart:
5. ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop/viewer.rs: DisplayRefresh { hz: f64 } op, with its Dart interface (desktop_api.dart), implementation and fake.
6. Windows runner (desktop_video.cpp): WindowRefreshHz(HWND): MonitorFromWindow on the Flutter view's HWND, GetMonitorInfoW for szDevice, QueryDisplayConfig(QDC_ONLY_ACTIVE_PATHS) with DISPLAYCONFIG_DEVICE_INFO_GET_SOURCE_NAME matching viewGdiDeviceName, returning that path's targetInfo.refreshRate exactly; else dmDisplayFrequency. Exposed as `refresh_hz`.
7. New ui/lib/src/ffi/display_refresh.dart: the window's display refresh; on Windows the runner's refresh_hz (bounded at 200 ms, falling back to the current value); elsewhere PlatformDispatcher's view display refreshRate.
8. desktop_store.dart: on macOS, Windows and Linux connect with that refresh as refresh_hz (desktop_store.dart:341, displayMaxHz); a PlatformDispatcher.onMetricsChanged listener (plus window focus and move on Windows) sends display_refresh whenever the value differs from the last sent, and once after connect. Android unchanged.
(The Mac runner's refreshHz stat already reports the window's screen, from viewer-decoder-stats.)
9. Docs: 'Viewer: newest decodable frame, fps cap and recovery' (remote-desktop.md:1643-1683) and the panel's refresh row; CHANGELOG bullet.
prs.verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop fps_cap` and `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib video` (lower at once, raise at once, override honoured, backlog lowers beneath the display, a backlog recovery sends release not max_fps; rounding); `cargo test -p pb-mapper-ffi` (op test); `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. From ui/: `flutter gen-l10n`, `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (store test with a fake channel answering 59.94; display_refresh sent on change). CI: android-check (`cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a clippy -p pb-mapper-ffi --locked -- -D warnings`), rust-windows-desktop, macos-app, linux-app; the Windows runner compiles only via release-ui.yml with windows_verify_only; nat-traversal.yml.

prs.name: linux-gpu-convert
prs.title: Linux viewer: keep decoded pictures on the GPU, converted in Flutter's GL context through an FlTextureGL (module ABI 2, dma-buf where available)
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire or the FFI. The runner-module C ABI goes from 1 to 2 (bump PB_VIDEO_MODULE_ABI to one above master's value at merge); both are built together and the ABI check (desktop_video.cc:109) rejects a stale module. File and symbol names stay.
prs.design:
Why. Today every hardware-decoded picture is downloaded to system memory (NV12: 3.1 MB at 1080p, 12.4 MB at 4K), converted to RGBA on the CPU by up to 4 videoconvert threads (desktop_video_gst.cc:88, 575-579), and re-specified into Flutter's texture as RGBA (8.3 or 33 MB). Estimated saving: 4-12 ms of CPU per 1080p picture and 15-40 ms per 4K picture across threads, which matters for laptop battery and thermals and makes 1440p or 4K at 60+ possible on iGPU laptops. Merged duplicate: R10-linux-gpu-convert (same goal; it also notes Flutter's Linux embedder takes at most 60 frames a second, so at 120 fps half of today's CPU conversions are discarded).

Design (the corrected one: no GstGL on the default path, the module stays GL-free and hands over the decoder's native picture; the runner converts in whatever GL context presents it, so no context bootstrap, no cross-context sync and no new runtime package):
1. Measurement commit first: module stats gain `timings.decode`; the harness prints CPU ms per decoded picture per thread from getrusage(RUSAGE_THREAD).
2. Module ABI 2 (desktop_video_module.h:79-111): pipeline appsrc -> parse -> decoder -> appsink with no videoconvert; appsink caps video/x-raw,format={NV12,I420}; add video/x-raw(memory:DMABuf),format=DMA_DRM,drm-format=<NV12 with the modifiers the presenter imports> only when the presenter reports dma-buf import and GStreamer >= 1.24; a decoder that offers none of these gets videoconvert to NV12. Candidates (166-223) accept decoders whose source pad offers system memory or DMABuf. create takes the presenter's capabilities (dma-buf import yes/no, modifier list). New describe(picture, PbVideoPlanes*) gives visible width/height and format, colour matrix and range from the caps (DefaultColorimetry keeps its BT.709 default), and per plane either {data, stride} or {dmabuf fd, offset, stride, drm fourcc, modifier}, using GstVideoMeta offsets so 1088-row surfaces crop. `pixels` is replaced by snapshot(picture, max_width, rgba out), which for system memory uses a GstVideoConverter scaling straight to <= 320 px. The module links gstreamer-allocators-1.0 (in libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev).
3. Runner GL helper, new ui/linux/runner/desktop_video_gl.cc (epoxy, which libgtk-3-dev brings): plane textures R8/RG8, or LUMINANCE/LUMINANCE_ALPHA on ES2 without EXT_texture_rg, updated with glTexSubImage2D (GL_UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH where available, else padded rows with scaled texture coordinates); or per-plane EGLImages (eglCreateImageKHR(EGL_LINUX_DMA_BUF_EXT, DRM_FORMAT_R8/GR88, modifier), cached per pooled buffer, glEGLImageTargetTexture2DOES). One shader pass (BT.709 or BT.601, limited or full range, from describe) into an RGBA8 GL_TEXTURE_2D through an FBO, saving and restoring every GL binding it touches as fl_compositor_opengl.cc:222-245, 348-358 do. An EGL fence after the pass; a picture returns to GStreamer only once its fence signalled (checked without waiting at the next call); hold at most 2 pictures. Capabilities read on the GTK thread at create without a context: eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT on GDK's native display (the EGLDisplay fl_opengl_manager.cc:47-61 obtains; initialize if needed, never eglTerminate), EGL_EXT_image_dma_buf_import(_modifiers), eglQueryDmaBufModifiersEXT for NV12; GL_OES_EGL_image confirmed at the first conversion, else the runner tells the module, which falls back to system memory at the next keyframe and asks for one once.
4. PbVideoTexture becomes an FlTextureGL subclass (desktop_video.cc:228-303): populate acquires the newest picture (the receipt), converts it and returns GL_TEXTURE_2D/GL_RGBA8 (suits Skia and Impeller); before the first picture a 1x1 black texture. For dma-buf pictures the helper refreshes an RGBA readback of <= 320 px at most once a second for snapshot. FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software keeps today's path.
5. Optional NVIDIA stage (NVDEC GLMemory through CUDA-GL interop) only if device numbers show NVDEC's download plus YUV upload still costs more than about 2 ms per 4K picture.
6. Build and CI: runner/CMakeLists.txt links epoxy; the module adds gstreamer-allocators-1.0; syntax-check.yml linux-app adds libegl1, libegl-mesa0 and libgles2 for the harness. No new runtime package in the user guide (no gstreamer1.0-gl).
7. Harness (ui/linux/test/desktop_video_test.cc:104-200): a surfaceless EGL ES2 context (llvmpipe) stands in for the raster thread and calls the helper; checks the converted texture is GL_TEXTURE_2D RGBA8 of the picture's size, glReadPixels of the converted test pattern matches videoconvert's RGBA of the same picture at PSNR >= 40 dB (BT.709 limited), the snapshot is non-uniform, and the software (libav I420) path decodes with no videoconvert.
8. Docs: 'macOS, iOS and Linux decoders' (remote-desktop.md:2204-2266); CHANGELOG bullet with device figures.
prs.verification: Here, from ui/: `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (no Dart change expected). CI linux-app (ubuntu-22.04): `flutter build linux --debug`, `bash scripts/build/check-linux-bundle.sh ui/build/linux/x64/debug/bundle`, `bash scripts/test/linux-desktop-video.sh --software` (GL helper correctness on llvmpipe: format, size, PSNR against videoconvert; decoded/s and presented/s for the 720p and 1080p clips before and after; CI CPU figures on llvmpipe are not gains).

prs.name: linux-presenting-gpu
prs.title: Linux viewer: decode on the GPU that presents the window (hybrid laptops, multi-GPU desktops)
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire or FFI. Module ABI bump (one above master's value at merge): probe and create take the presenting render node.
prs.design:
Why. Candidates are ordered hardware first, then registry rank (desktop_video_gst.cc:187-223, sorted at 219-221), with no regard for which GPU renders the window. On a PRIME render-offload laptop (Intel/AMD iGPU drawing, NVIDIA dGPU asleep) or a desktop with two VA devices, whichever of nvh264dec, vah264dec or varenderD129h264dec ranks higher wins: NVDEC keeps the dGPU awake for the whole session (several watts) and sends every picture across PCIe and back, and a dma-buf import across GPUs (linux-gpu-convert) fails or falls back.

1. On the GTK thread, before the `decoders` probe task starts, find the presenting GPU's DRM render node: eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT on GDK's native display (Wayland or X11; the EGLDisplay fl_opengl_manager.cc:47-61 uses; initialize if needed, never eglTerminate), eglQueryDisplayAttribEXT(EGL_DEVICE_EXT), then eglQueryDeviceStringEXT(EGL_DRM_RENDER_NODE_FILE_EXT), falling back to EGL_DRM_DEVICE_FILE_EXT.
2. Pass the node to probe and create.
3. Candidates order hardware decoders by 'on the presenting device', then rank: va per-device factories (va<renderDNNN>h264dec) name their node, the default vah264dec is the first render node; nvcodec maps cuda-device-id -> PCI bus id -> /dev/dri/by-path/pci-<bus>-render; vaapih264dec uses LIBVA's default node.
4. A decoder on another GPU stays a fallback. The probe's text names the device, so the quality panel shows it.
5. Docs: the Linux decoder section; CHANGELOG bullet.
prs.verification: CI linux-app: `flutter build linux --debug`, `bash scripts/build/check-linux-bundle.sh ui/build/linux/x64/debug/bundle`, `bash scripts/test/linux-desktop-video.sh --software` (single llvmpipe device: the ordering falls back unchanged). A unit test of the candidate ordering as a pure function of (candidates, node) in the harness. Here: `dart format`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` if any Dart changes.
prs.measurement: Device-only: an Intel+NVIDIA laptop (PRIME on-demand) on battery, 1080p60 for 10 minutes, before and after: chosen decoder (G_MESSAGES_DEBUG=pb-mapper-video), `cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/<dGPU>/power/runtime_status` (expect 'suspended' after), `nvidia-smi -q -d POWER`, battery discharge from `upower -i`, CPU from pidstat; an AMD iGPU+dGPU desktop with two VA nodes; on Ubuntu 22.04 (GStreamer 1.20) record `gst-inspect-1.0 vah264dec | grep Rank`. Record under docs/benchmarks/.

prs.name: linux-video-plane
prs.title: Linux viewer: present video on a GTK GL plane under a transparent FlView, off Flutter's fixed 60 Hz clock
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire, FFI or module ABI. The runner channel `pb_mapper/desktop_video`: the create reply gains `plane`, a new `place` method, `grey` implemented for the plane, and stats gain planeIntervalP50Ms/P95Ms and refreshIntervalMs. The Dart DesktopVideoTexture interface and its fakes change with it.
prs.design:
Why. Every Linux viewer presents at most 60 fps through Flutter's fixed timer (proven from the pinned 3.44.9 sources); each picture waits for that timer, unsynchronised with the display (mean about 8 ms), then raster, populate and compose, then GTK's frame clock. With a plane: 120 Hz+ monitors on Smooth get up to 120 fps on Wayland (GNOME, KDE, wlroots) and Mutter X11; every user loses one unsynchronised wait plus 1-4 ms of Flutter work (estimate 8-13 ms off the mean at 60 Hz); on X11 a video picture no longer triggers a full-window glReadPixels.

1. Runner (my_application.cc:59-78): the FlView becomes the overlay child of a GtkOverlay whose main child is a new PbVideoPlane, a GtkGLArea in ui/linux/runner/desktop_video_plane.cc (has-alpha FALSE, auto-render). The plane starts hidden and the FlView background stays opaque black. Only while a plane-backed viewer has placed a visible rect: show the plane and fl_view_set_background_color(#00000000) (takes effect on the next draw, fl_view.cc:862-867); revert on visible=false or dispose. Outside a session nothing changes.
2. UI thread: fl_dart_project_set_ui_thread_policy(project, FL_UI_THREAD_POLICY_RUN_ON_SEPARATE_THREAD) (public in 3.44.9, fl_dart_project.cc:121) as its own commit, measured A/B; keep it only if the plane's p95 interval improves under Dart load.
3. Plane render (GTK thread): if a new picture is pending, acquire it through module->acquire (the receipt) and convert it with linux-gpu-convert's GL helper into an RGBA8 texture in GDK's context (EGL on Wayland, so dma-buf import works; GLX on X11, the YUV-upload path, reporting 'no dma-buf' to the module for this presenter); draw one quad into the placed rect with a scissor to the clip (GLSL 150 core, or ES 1.00 when gdk_gl_context_get_use_es); keep the last RGBA texture so a redraw caused by FlView or an overlay never re-acquires or re-converts. In plane mode frame_ready never calls fl_texture_registrar_mark_texture_frame_available: it sets an atomic pending flag and once per pending picture g_main_context_invoke_full(G_PRIORITY_HIGH) runs gtk_widget_queue_draw_area on the placed rect.
4. Stall fallback: a picture pending 100 ms with no plane render is acquired by a GTK timeout (the receipt) without drawing and kept for the next paint (well under the 700 ms watchdog; keeps receipts when a Wayland window is covered).
5. Grey still: implement `grey` (the DesktopVideoTexture method mac-viewer-layer added) as a saturation matrix uniform in the plane's shader; GreyStill already calls it for native presenters (extend its condition to `plane`).
6. Dart hole: viewer_stage.dart:185-197 draws a NativeVideoHole (new native_video_hole.dart) instead of Texture when picture.plane is set: a leaf render object with isRepaintBoundary true; its paint calls context.setWillChangeHint() (never raster-cached) and draws the picture rect intersected with the stage clip with BlendMode.clear, clearing the ground desktop_viewer.dart:275 and touch_viewer.dart:397 painted; the cursors and overlays paint after it as today. From paint it computes getTransformTo(null) x size x devicePixelRatio (GDK's integer scale) and, when that or the clip changes, sends `place` {textureId, visible, x, y, w, h, clipX, clipY, clipW, clipH} after the frame; it sends visible=false when it was not painted in a frame, including route transitions drawn inside an OpacityLayer.
7. Channel: create answers {textureId, plane}; the plane goes to the first texture only, only if the GtkGLArea realized with no gtk_gl_area_get_error, never under FLUTTER_LINUX_RENDERER=software; every refusal stays on the Flutter texture. dispose hides the plane and restores the opaque background. DesktopVideoTexture gains place(); the channel texture and test fakes change in the same commit.
8. Stats: planeIntervalP50Ms/P95Ms from gdk_frame_clock_get_timings (presentation_time, or frame_time where absent) and refreshIntervalMs from gdk_frame_clock_get_refresh_info.
9. Upgrade note in the docs: when the Flutter pin moves to 3.50+ (Wayland subsurface renderer, X11 fl_opengl_frame), re-verify that Flutter's subsurface buffer keeps alpha over the plane before shipping.
10. Docs: 'The app's video path' and 'macOS, iOS and Linux decoders' (2204-2266); CHANGELOG bullet.

prs.name: mac-viewer-enhance
prs.title: macOS viewer: optional GPU enhancement of an enlarged picture (clamped Catmull-Rom plus luma-only sharpening) through a CAMetalLayer, and the shared 'sharpen enlarged picture' preference
prs.protocol_changes: None: app-internal channel method `enhance {textureId, level}`.
prs.design:
Why. A 1920x1080 or 2560x1440 host full-screen on a 3024x1964 to 3456x2234 Retina panel or a 4K/5K external is enlarged 1.2-1.8x bilinearly today, so text is soft. airhand offers luma sharpening with peaks off/low/medium/high = 0/-0.06/-0.1/-0.14 (client/src/lib/enhance.ts:22) and plans the presenter by on-screen size. Off by default, it costs nothing; on, one or two GPU passes at display size (airhand quotes about 0.5 ms on an RTX 4080 laptop; unmeasured on this M6).

Builds on mac-viewer-layer, macOS only:
1. A second presenter mode, active only while enhancement is on and the on-screen pixel size is at least the picture's on both axes (below that the plain YUV layer, as airhand's renderPlan). The on-screen size is the layer bounds converted to the window's root layer times backingScaleFactor, recomputed in layout() and when the mutator transform changes.
2. A CAMetalLayer beside the plain content layer; a switch toggles their isHidden in one main-thread transaction, so the picture never blanks. CAMetalLayer: .bgra8Unorm, sRGB colourspace, framebufferOnly, maximumDrawableCount 3, drawableSize = on-screen pixels.
3. A presenter thread with a newest-wins slot: the feed thread puts the decoded 420v picture there and returns at once. The presenter thread wraps both planes through CVMetalTextureCache (R8, RG8; zero copy); pass 1 converts with the BT.709 limited-range matrix and no transfer conversion (same sRGB look as the plain layer) and upscales with 9-tap Catmull-Rom clamped to the 4 nearest texels into a private intermediate texture (skipped at exactly 1:1); pass 2 applies CAS-style luma-only sharpening with airhand's peaks into the drawable; commit with present. The receipt and timings.present are taken at the scheduled present. It keeps the last picture and redraws when the geometry or level changes. Shaders compile at run time from a source string (MTLDevice.makeLibrary(source:)), so no .metal resource or project-file change.
4. Snapshot keeps using the decoded buffer.
5. Dart: a per-device preference 'Sharpen enlarged picture' (off, low, medium, high; default off) in viewer_prefs.dart and the viewer's Display menu (viewer_menus.dart), sent through `enhance {textureId, level}`, offered only when the texture has a native presenter. linux-plane-scaling reuses the same preference for its plane. Strings in both locales; icons from AppIcons.
6. Docs and CHANGELOG.

prs.name: linux-plane-scaling
prs.title: Linux viewer plane: area-averaged downscaling always, and the shared sharpen-enlarged setting (clamped Catmull-Rom plus luma sharpening) when enlarging
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire. The runner channel's `place` gains {filter, sharpen}.
prs.design:
Why. Shrinking a 1440p or 4K remote into a window below 0.5x with bilinear and no mipmaps aliases text; enlarging 1080p to a 1440p or 4K full screen is soft. Quality only; nothing changes for bandwidth or latency; it applies only where the plane is active (the Flutter Texture fallback keeps bilinear).

1. Two passes in the plane: YUV to RGBA at the picture's own size (the GL helper's pass), then a scale pass into the placed rect by scale s: s = 1 a 1:1 copy; s < 1, always on, an area filter of up to 3x3 bilinear taps spaced 1/s apart, and below s = 1/3 generate mipmaps of the RGBA texture once per new picture (never per redraw) and sample trilinearly; s > 1 bilinear by default, and when the user picks a level, Catmull-Rom from 9 bilinear taps clamped to the 4 nearest texels plus CAS on luma only with peaks 0/-0.06/-0.1/-0.14 (airhand client/src/lib/enhance.ts:22).
2. Shaders in a GLSL 150 core variant and an ES 1.00/3.00 variant chosen by gdk_gl_context_get_use_es.
3. Dart: the 'Sharpen enlarged picture' preference from mac-viewer-enhance, sent with `place` as {filter, sharpen}; the Display menu offers it while the plane is active.
4. Docs and CHANGELOG.

prs.name: viewer-scroll
prs.title: Scrolling: one wheel notch is one host notch on every viewer, high-resolution (1/120-notch) scrolling by capability, and trackpad momentum carried to the host
prs.protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: host capability `wheel_hires` (from a new BackendCaps.hires_wheel, listed in BackendCaps::values()); new `Input::Scroll { horizontal: i32, vertical: i32, continuous: bool }` in 1/120-notch units (continuous serde default, skipped when false), |v| <= 12000 in Input::validate, sent only to a host that listed wheel_hires (Viewer::input returns NotOffered otherwise). Helper pipe: Input::Scroll crosses it and StartCaps gains hires_wheel: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names (.v<n>). No FFI export change (the existing input op carries Input JSON). Runner channel pb_mapper/desktop_pointer gains `wheel_lines` (Windows).
prs.design:
Why. (a) remote_surface.dart turns every PointerScrollEvent into notches at kWheelPxPerNotch = 30 logical px (:19, :229-238), but each embedder reports one wheel notch as a different distance: Windows lines x 100/3 physical px (flutter_window.cc:468-478, 798-808; flutter_windows_view.cc:660-661), i.e. 100/DPR logical at 3 lines; macOS 40 logical per line (FlutterViewController.mm:735-757); Linux 53 (fl_scrolling_manager.cc:108). One Windows notch at 100% sends 3,3,4,3 notches (9-12 lines on a Windows host); macOS and Linux send 1,1,2 and 2,2,1 patterns. (b) A 30 px trackpad move becomes a whole notch: 3 lines (about 100 px) on a Windows host, 1 line on a Mac host, so remote content jumps in steps and scrolls about 3x too fast on Windows hosts. (c) Flutter drops OS scroll momentum on every desktop platform (macOS skips momentum-phase events, FlutterViewController.mm:614-625; Windows suppresses DirectManipulation inertia, direct_manipulation.cc:73, 152; GTK/libinput produce none), and pb-mapper reads raw PanZoom in a Listener (remote_surface.dart:213-226), so a fling stops dead on the remote computer. airhand forwards OS momentum as wheel events (client/src/lib/input.ts:518-530).

1. Notch fidelity (R4-wheel-notch-fidelity; every host, old ones included, no protocol): for a mouse-kind PointerScrollEvent, notches = delta / pxPerNotch with pxPerNotch per viewer platform: Windows 100 x lines/3 / devicePixelRatio, macOS 40, Linux 53; the carry stays. `lines` comes from `wheel_lines` on the Windows runner's pb_mapper/desktop_pointer channel (SPI_GETWHEELSCROLLLINES; 3 if the call fails). Trackpad PanZoom and trackpad-kind scroll keep their own distance per notch.
2. Units (R4-hires-scroll): 120 = one notch = 100 logical px of continuous travel. Protocol as above; Outbound::submit sums a single-Scroll batch onto a tail Scroll of the same generation and continuity (beside outbound.rs:249-261), so a trackpad flood never fills the 512-event queue.
3. Dart _wheelBy, when capabilities contain wheel_hires: PointerPanZoomUpdate and trackpad-kind PointerScrollEvent -> units = px x 1.2, continuous; a mouse PointerScrollEvent -> units = notches x 120 (notches per step 1), continuous = false; a carry per axis. Without the capability send today's notches at the corrected per-platform notch size.
4. Host: Injector::scroll(h, v, continuous) has a default that accumulates whole notches into wheel(); native.rs maps Scroll; thread C re-aims the pointer before Scroll as before Wheel (worker/control.rs:458-470). Windows: one SendInput carrying MOUSEEVENTF_WHEEL mouseData = -vertical and/or MOUSEEVENTF_HWHEEL mouseData = horizontal (only the nonzero ones). macOS: continuous posts CGScrollEventUnit::Pixel with px = units / 1.2 (points) with a carry and kCGScrollWheelEventIsContinuous = 1; discrete stays CGScrollEventUnit::Line at units/120 lines with a carry (one line per notch as today). The synthetic backend lists the capability so desktop_ui_host logs Scroll.
5. Momentum (R4-trackpad-momentum), Dart in RemoteSurface: track PanZoomUpdate pan deltas with a VelocityTracker (trackpad kind, event timestamps); on PointerPanZoomEnd above kMinFlingVelocity run a Ticker-driven decay with the viewer platform's physics (macOS's 0.998/ms deceleration as BouncingScrollSimulation's friction; a ClampingScrollSimulation-like curve on Windows and Linux); each tick sends the integrated delta through _wheelBy (continuous Scroll units with wheel_hires, else notches with the carry). Cancel on PointerScrollInertiaCancelEvent, a new PanZoomStart, a pointer down, a discrete wheel event, focus or control loss, or a generation change. Outbound summing bounds the queue.
6. Helper: bump as above, one record of the bump in the remote-desktop.md protocol history.
7. Docs and CHANGELOG: the Platforms table (remote-desktop.md:1132), the Constants Input row, the 'a notch per 30 px' text (:237-238); the user-guide pair if it mentions scrolling or the helper update.
Legacy guard: if a classic Win32 listbox or a Java Swing list fails to scroll under continuous input on a device, add a viewer setting to turn smooth scroll off.

From ui/: `flutter gen-l10n`, `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (conversion per target platform with debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride for Windows at DPR 1, 1.5, 2, macOS and Linux: one notch event yields exactly one host notch; capability gating; momentum decay, distance within platform bounds and every cancellation). prs.name: standby-session
prs.title: A warm standby session on the other path: survive a dead direct path in about 1.5 s and upgrade a relayed session to direct
prs.protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: capability `standby` both ways; optional `Accepted.ticket` (32 bytes from ring's SystemRandom, base64url) and `Authenticate.standby_for`, each sent only to a peer that listed the capability (serde default, omitted when unset). No relay wire or DIRECT_VERSION change. SDK: a #[doc(hidden)] `Client::connect_tcp_direct` (no PathPolicy variant, no ConnectOptions field). No FFI or Dart change (logic inside Viewer); no helper-pipe change (HostStatus keeps its shape).
prs.design:
Why. A direct-specific failure (a NAT rebinding or firewall that kills the punched path while the relay is alive) costs an estimated 8-9 s outage today, with the room emptying and display modes restored in between; a relayed session that fell back transiently stays on the relay for its life (the deployed TCP relay measured a 194 ms median ping, docs/remote-desktop.md:2533). Two ordinary sessions, no splice, no new ALPN.

1. When standbys open. A relay standby opens only for an internet-direct primary (punched or port-mapped QUIC), never for LAN QUIC or LAN TCP. A direct-only standby opens only after a NegotiationTimeout, NegotiationFailed or Unreachable fallback; it obeys the shared cooldown (direct-cooldown) and the NetworkHints generation, is never tried after NotOffered, reuses one Consumer and Network per Viewer across attempts, and records its own outcome (it must not log session_path_selected path=relay or count as a fallback).
2. Protocol as above.
3. Host acceptor: check the token first in constant time, then the ticket in constant time over SHA-256 digests. A standby takes a standby permit (one per active slot), starts paused, causes no room keyframe, and does not appear in HostStatus or in peer cursors.
4. Promotion is a Resume on the standby. Under the room lock the room moves display-mode ownership, the admission lease and the ticket to the promoted slot, then ends the primary with End::Closed. Held input is released at the primary's end, failing closed. The resume IDR is forced; reset_baseline runs only if the route differs. Restore runs when the pair ends.
5. Viewer, new viewer/standby.rs: promote at once on a transport error on the primary, or when the primary has had no bytes for max(1.5 s, 4 x base RTT) while the standby received at least one message in that interval; promote a committed direct standby at once (default order, no RTT gate). Attach the standby to the VideoSink with a discontinuity so it waits for the IDR (sink.rs:377-386), then swap the metrics connection slot; document that an earlier subscribe_metrics stream ends at a switch.
6. Telemetry, trace only: desktop_viewer_promoted{cause, outage_ms}, desktop_viewer_standby{route, outcome}.
7. Established direct sessions keep belonging to the endpoints: coordinator loss, revocation or relay rejection never close them (CLAUDE.md invariants unchanged).
8. Docs: the user-guide pair, the remote-desktop.md lifecycle and constants, a relay operator note (one extra relay stream per internet-direct viewer); CHANGELOG bullet. Keep each capability list within MAX_CAPABILITIES.

prs.name: helper-push
prs.title: Helper protocol: the worker pushes encoded units, fresh-picture notices (with present age) and pointer updates; thread C stops long-polling the pipe
prs.protocol_changes: Helper pipe: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names (.v<n>). Between replies the worker may send tagged records, all deny_unknown_fields: {kind:'unit', generation, video: VideoFormat, pending} followed by its bytes record; {kind:'fresh', presented_ago_us, presented_count}; {kind:'pointer', cursor, shape_serial}. Replies are tagged {kind:'reply', ...Response}; the Video reply gains presented_ago_us: Option<u32> and presented_count: Option<u8> for the submitted picture (serde default, omitted when None). Request gains Stream{on}; Request::Video loses wait_ms (DRAIN_WAIT_MAX_MS goes). Both ends validate: a unit is at most ipc::MAX_FRAME, its generation matches the host's expected context, pending <= 64, the pointer lies inside the display, ages over 1 s are ignored, unknown kinds are rejected. Desktop wire and ALPN unchanged.
prs.design:
Why. Every privileged Windows session ('Turn on remote control' selects Access::Privileged, ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop/host.rs:521-525) pays pipe round trips while active of up to about 500/s, each crossing two pipes and the service relay and costing 3-5 desktop verifications plus AcquireNextFrame in the worker; units arrive 0.3-1 ms late through the drain long-poll; input queues behind that long-poll (0-4 ms); and the helper path gets no present stamps, so the anchored pacer (capture-anchored-pacing) runs on the grid there. Land after win-mf-output-events and win-present-waiter so the worker is event-driven end to end.

1. Worker (oop/server.rs, helper/worker.rs): serve_bound waits on a crate Waiter (platform/windows/waiter.rs) bound to its backend's Waker through PlatformBackend::bind; the exchange task notifies it after each try_send. Each iteration serves queued requests first; then, while Stream{on}: drain finished units and send Unit plus its bytes record (one vectored write_record from helper-pipe-transfer); when the armed source has published a fresh picture, send Fresh{presented_ago_us, presented_count} once per armed present (the age computed just before writing); every 16 ms read the pointer and send Pointer only when it or the shape serial changed. The worker's timer guard follows Stream{on}.
2. Arming: a submitting Video request that finds nothing new leaves the worker's source armed, with the capture thread waiting for a present; no hot_ms.
3. Host (oop/client.rs): one I/O thread owns the current_thread runtime and the NamedPipeClient; call() sends (Request, oneshot) and blocks. The I/O thread demuxes: Reply -> the oneshot; Unit -> a VecDeque bounded at ENCODER_DEPTH + 2 (overflow is a protocol error, NotConnected); Fresh -> a flag, the stamp converted against its receive Instant, and Waker::wake; Pointer -> the cached cursor and serial. bind keeps the Waker; drain_poll and capture_poll -> None; capture_idle_until as MacVideo's; drain_video pops with no pipe call and drops units of another generation; pending = last reported + queued; submitted_picture() returns the Video reply's presented age converted at receipt (this is the helper half of R3-present-anchoring). Input replies keep their post-injection cursor read, which thread C's own-move echo logic needs.
4. Thread C (worker/capture.rs): remove HELPER_DRAIN_WAIT_MAX and DRAIN_WAIT_MAX_MS.
5. platform/synthetic.rs push mode (from capture-anchored-pacing) drives protocol tests over a duplex.
6. Optional, only if the device shows the Fresh-to-submit round trip above about 0.5 ms: let an armed worker submit at the present and push Submitted{presented_ago_us} (needs a thread C hook for a deferred tick).
7. Docs: remote-desktop.md protocol paragraph and history; docs/architecture.md; the user-guide pair (English and Chinese) together; CHANGELOG bullet that the Windows desktop service must be updated (Update installs it).

prs.title: AV1 negotiated by an `av1` capability, decoded on Windows, macOS (M3+) and Linux viewers, with a clip host that serves it
prs.protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: viewer capability `av1`; VideoCodec value `av1` used only in Accepted.codec to a viewer that listed av1; `av1` in `codecs` is InvalidRequest (like h265). BackendCaps gains a public `av1: bool` (a backend that encodes AV1 without a probe); oop/proto.rs's From<&BackendCaps>/From<StartCaps> ignore it (no helper wire change, no bump here). Why. QoS caps bits per frame on every link (Balanced 1080p: 66,667-133,333 bits per frame), so codec efficiency shows on a LAN too. Viewers offer every codec they decode either way.
2. Host-side eligibility here: thread C (worker.rs:293-295) treats AV1 as available when describe(false)'s caps.av1 is set; no probe in this PR.
3. Bitstream: codec/obu.rs parses in place into a reused Vec, requires has_size_field, rejects the forbidden bit, truncation and more than 4096 OBUs, defines a keyframe as a shown KEY_FRAME; SequenceHeader works like ParameterSets and is prepended after a leading TD to a keyframe that lacks it; sizes bounded.
4. Supervisor: Retry.drop: Option<VideoCodec>, giving the reconnect chain AV1 -> H.265 -> H.264 after an encoder failure.
5. Clip host: crates/pb-mapper/examples/desktop_ui_host.rs serves an AV1 OBU clip (caps.av1 true, keyframes from codec/obu.rs); ui/native/pb_mapper_ffi/src/desktop_video/test_source.rs gets its own sequence-header size parse. Darwin (DesktopVideo.swift): 'av01' FourCC behind #available(macOS 14, iOS 17); an OBU splitter that drops TDs; an av1C built from the sequence header; the probe answers VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported('av01'); confirm with the fixture on this M6 whether VTDecompressionSession needs VTRegisterSupplementalVideoDecoderIfAvailable. Works in both presenters (layer and texture).

prs.name: relative-pointer
prs.title: Relative pointer mode with pointer lock for apps that hide and recenter the host pointer (games, 3D viewports)
prs.protocol_changes: Desktop wire, ALPN unchanged: host capability `relative_pointer` (from BackendCaps.relative_pointer, Windows and macOS injectors and the synthetic backend); `Input::MoveBy { dx: i32, dy: i32 }` with |d| <= 4096, sent only to a host that listed it (Viewer::input NotOffered otherwise). Helper pipe: Input::MoveBy and StartCaps.relative_pointer cross it: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names. Runner channel pb_mapper/desktop_pointer gains lock/unlock and posts raw deltas. No FFI export change.
prs.design:
Why. Raw-input games and 3D viewports on a Windows host get no motion at all (SetCursorPos is not input), and apps that hide and recenter the pointer (FPS cameras, Blender or CAD orbit with continuous grab) fight absolute moves on both hosts: the view jumps or stops at the picture's edge. airhand switches to relative moves with pointer lock (client/src/lib/input.ts:1-40; crates/airhand-proto session.rs:30-55; host/input/macos.rs:236-243).

1. Protocol and host: capability and Input::MoveBy as above; Outbound::submit sums a single MoveBy onto a tail MoveBy (outbound.rs:249-261). Injector::pointer_by: Windows relative SendInput MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE (the OS pointer follows speed and precision settings; raw-input readers get exact deltas); macOS MouseMoved (Dragged while a button is held) at the current location plus the delta with MouseEventDeltaX/Y set and the injector's cached position cleared, as airhand host/input/macos.rs:236-243. native.rs maps MoveBy; thread C records no injected echo for it and starts the 2 ms hot cursor sample after MoveBy (pointer-cadence's shape_due extended to positions) so the painted pointer follows within about 2 ms. WinCursor::read reports a null hCursor as hidden (pure function test).
2. Dart: DesktopStore.send sums MoveBy into the pending slot within the 4 ms gate; NOT_FRESH drops MoveBy rather than keeping it. In relative mode the viewer takes every cursor report (no cursor_sequence set-aside); RemoteCursorLayer paints the host pointer; the OS pointer is hidden and locked.
3. Modes (airhand input.ts:1-40), a per-device preference in viewer_prefs.dart and the viewer menu: auto (lock when the host reports the pointer hidden while a button is held, or hidden through 300 ms of movement; unlock when it shows and every button is up; Windows' hide-while-typing never locks because a pointer reappearing within 300 ms does not count); desktop (never lock); game (always lock). A 1 s Esc hold releases the lock, and so does focus loss.
4. Runners (desktop_pointer files from native-cursor), each accumulating raw deltas and posting them at most once per loop turn: Windows ClipCursor to the picture, ShowCursor(FALSE), RegisterRawInputDevices on the top-level window for relative WM_INPUT (handled from flutter_window.cpp's message hook); macOS CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(false), NSCursor.hide, an NSEvent local monitor reading deltaX/deltaY; Linux X11 gdk_seat_grab with XInput2 XI_RawMotion (adds libxi-dev), Linux Wayland zwp_locked_pointer_v1 with zwp_relative_pointer_v1, code generated by wayland-scanner in CMake (adds wayland-protocols to the linux-app CI job). Every lock path restores association and visibility on unlock, dispose and focus loss.
5. Docs: input section and capability list, the user-guide pair (modes; helper update); CHANGELOG bullet. Keep capability lists within MAX_CAPABILITIES.

From ui/: `flutter gen-l10n` (untranslated stays {}), `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test tool`, `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`, `flutter test` (auto-lock rules including hide-while-typing, MoveBy summing in the gate, the NOT_FRESH drop, Esc hold, focus loss); icons from AppIcons. macOS app build here. prs.name: av1-windows-host
prs.title: Windows host: encode AV1 with the GPU's Media Foundation encoder for viewers that listed av1, probed concurrently and cached

Helper pipe: Request::Encodes{codec} replaces H265{}, Response.encodes answers it, VideoCodec av1 in Video requests and responses, EncoderFailed{Av1}: bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names. prs.design:
Why. Windows hosts with an AV1 encoder (RTX 40/50, Intel Arc and Core Ultra, RDNA3+) paired with viewers that decode AV1 but not HEVC run H.264 Baseline today; AV1 at the same bits per frame should be materially sharper. Size per vendor is unmeasured; latency change negligible (NVIDIA HEVC already encodes 1080p in 1.65 ms mean); smaller IDRs shorten keyframe recovery. Merged duplicate: R3-av1-encode.

1. Probe (no serial cold probe per helper session): add a provided `Backend::probe_codec(&mut self, codec: VideoCodec) -> Result<bool> { Ok(false) }` forwarded in all five deny(missing_trait_methods) impls; thread C (worker.rs:293-295) probes AV1 only when the viewer offers av1 and H.265 will not be used (the viewer lacks h265, the H.265 probe said no, or H265_FAILED), on its own answer channel so H.265 never waits for it. PlatformBackend answers from P::Video::encodes(display, codec); the in-process cache (probe.rs PROBED) becomes (adapter, codec). The helper worker probes H.265 and AV1 on two threads at once, each answering its own Response field; RemoteBackend's process-wide cache from helper-probe-cache becomes {(AdapterKey, codec) -> bool}.
2. codec.rs: subtype MFVideoFormat_AV1 with no MF_MT_MPEG2_PROFILE; the same low-latency, CBR and infinite-GOP read-back as H.264/H.265; the B-frame and reorder rules; encoder_available(luid, codec).
3. collect (video/mod.rs): enforce shown_frames() == 1 per temporal unit through codec/obu.rs; a violation is a codec_error that latches AV1; keyframes and the sequence-header prepend as defined in av1-viewers.
4. Failure latches per codec [H265, Av1] in worker/capture.rs fail(): codec_error maps Av1 to EncoderFailed{Av1}; events desktop_av1_failed and desktop_av1_probe; the viewer's supervisor chain AV1 -> H.265 -> H.264 already exists.

prs.name: win-phase-locked-decimation
prs.title: Windows host: at a pace that is an integer fraction of the refresh, capture every k-th present as it lands instead of a stale picture at a grid tick
prs.protocol_changes: Desktop wire none. Helper pipe: Request::Video and Stream gain `not_before_in_us: Option<u32>` (relative to now, serde default): bump HELPER_PROTOCOL to one above master's value at merge with both pipe names. Public SDK: one provided Backend method (semver-minor).
prs.design:
Why. capture-anchored-pacing anchors only when the pace equals the present rate. When the pace is an integer fraction of the refresh (Quality's 30 on 60 Hz, Balanced 60 on a 120 Hz host, 72 on 144 Hz, 40 on 120 Hz) the grid takes whatever picture is newest at its tick, a picture up to a source period old. Model (scratchpad notes r9/align.py, continuous content, 2 ms polls): mean present-to-capture wait 3.2-8.8 ms -> 0.55-0.9 ms; mean event latency 60 Hz/30: 15.8-17.1 -> 9.1 ms; 120 Hz/60: 8.0-8.3 -> 4.8 ms; 144/72: 6.7 -> 4.0 ms; 120/40: 11.8 -> 8.9 ms; frame rate unchanged within 0.5%. On the Mac, mac-capture-cadence already makes ScreenCaptureKit deliver every k-th vsync at an exact multiple, and the anchored pacer takes each on arrival, so this PR is Windows-only.

1. Lock (pacer.rs): the source presents continuously (the last 4 dated captures each took k new presents, from Presented.presents); the source period is known (DXGI_OUTDUPL_DESC.ModeDesc refresh); k = round(refresh / pace) >= 2 and |refresh/k - pace| < pace/64.
2. While locked the next capture targets the predicted k-th present after the last one taken, at last_stamp + k x Pd: the window opens Pd/4 before it; a waiting picture stamped earlier than predicted - Pd/4 is not taken while the prediction is still due; it is taken anyway at predicted + 1 ms if nothing newer came; the floor stays last + 3P/4, so the rate is bounded by the display.
3. Thread C passes the target as a 'not before' stamp through a provided Backend method (forwarded in the five impls), an internal VideoSource argument (DXGI's capture thread returns Unchanged for an older picture), and through the helper as Request::Video/Stream.not_before_in_us.
4. Non-integer ratios (45 on 60 Hz, 60 on 144 Hz) and non-continuous content keep today's behaviour byte for byte.
5. Docs: rule 2 of the performance model; CHANGELOG with device figures.
prs.verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`: pacer and worker tests with a dated Fake at 60 Hz/30, 120 Hz/60 and 144 Hz/72 plus non-integer ratios: locked p95 wait < 2 ms; rate <= pace x 64/63; the stale picture is still taken by predicted + 1 ms when no present comes; non-locked behaviour identical to the grid; oop round trip of not_before_in_us. `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI rust-windows-desktop, nat-traversal.yml.

Record under docs/benchmarks/<date>-capture-pacing/.

prs.name: direct-cooldown
prs.title: Share the direct-fallback cooldown across connect_tcp calls per Client and service
prs.protocol_changes: None.
prs.design:
Why. CLAUDE.md's invariant says that after a pre-commit fallback the consumer pauses direct (10 s doubling to 5 min), so an unpunchable path costs one attempt, not one per connection. Today the cooldown lives in each Consumer, and every connect_tcp (each viewer session and reconnect) builds a new one, so every reconnect behind a symmetric NAT or blocked UDP pays about 2-3 s of punch setup again; the app's reconnect backoff of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 s (desktop_store.dart:22) falls inside the cooldown.

1. ClientInner (sdk/client.rs:36) gets `direct_memory: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<DirectMemory>>`: at most 64 entries, evicting expired ones first, keyed by (relay endpoint identity, namespace, service key); each entry holds the Cooldown, the TCP Cooldown and the network generation of its last back-off.
2. run_owned_stream (client/mod.rs:408) passes the entry into Consumer::new; cooldown() and tcp_cooldown() read through it and report it cleared when the generation differs. A direct success clears it, as today; diagnostics.direct_cooldown is reported as today.
3. Listener workers are unchanged (they already share one Consumer).
4. Step 2, sharing the consumer Network (UDP sockets, STUN result, port-mapping lease) per entry with a 60 s idle expiry, only if the existing SetupTimings diagnostics show discovery plus mapping of at least 100 ms per connect on devices.

prs.name: host-direct-bbr
prs.title: BBR on the desktop host's direct QUIC (the video sender), once receipt-driven control owns the rate
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire (congestion control is sender-local). No public RegisterOptions field: a #[doc(hidden)] Client method; no Node, CLI or helper-pipe change.
prs.design:
Why. On WAN direct paths with random loss of about 0.1% or more and RTTs of 50 ms or more (cross-border links, cellular hotspots, long-haul paths), Cubic's loss response caps the video sender's throughput and slows IDRs and scroll bursts. BBR is not limited by random loss. Nothing changes on LAN or clean paths. On policed uplinks only receipt control protects the path, hence the ship order.

1. A #[doc(hidden)] Client method, e.g. `register_with_sender_congestion(request, options, SenderCongestion::Bbr)`, threading a crate-private choice through DirectPolicy (direct_policy.rs:17-24) to the provider Network::new (direct/provider.rs:301), identity.server and transport(), which sets congestion_controller_factory(Arc::new(quinn::congestion::BbrConfig::default())). pb-mapper-desktop's host.rs:383 calls it, compiled in, so the Windows background host needs no helper-pipe field.
2. The consumer side, generic tunnels and the relay QUIC carrier stay on Cubic.
3. DirectLink (non_exhaustive) gains a controller label so device traces tell the two apart.
4. pb-mapper-testkit: new lossy_udp(loss, delay, rate_bps): a per-direction ordered queue after airhand crates/airhand-link/src/lib.rs:85-150, with a seeded PRNG and raised socket buffers; test-only (its per-packet copies never reach a data path).
5. New example crates/pb-mapper-desktop/examples/direct_cc_bench.rs: two quinn endpoints with pb-mapper's direct TransportConfig through the forwarder; 60 fps P-frames of 8.3 KB and a 150 KB IDR every 2 s under the credit window, with echoed receipts.
6. Ship only if the bench gates below pass; otherwise keep Cubic and record why.
7. Docs: transport section (sender congestion control); CHANGELOG bullet.
prs.verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-client -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features`, `cargo test -p pb-mapper-cli --all-features --test e2e direct`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`; `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI nat-traversal.yml on Linux (`cargo build -p pb-mapper-cli --features port-mapping`, `sudo python3 scripts/test_nat_traversal.py --binary target/debug/pb-mapper`), rust-windows-desktop, node-e2e.

Ship only if IDR p95 falls and delivered rate rises at 0.1-1% loss, and in the policer case p99 frame latency and loss do not rise with receipt control on. prs.name: relay-tcp-tuning
prs.title: Linux relay: disable TCP slow start after idle (Docker sysctl, opt-in install step, startup notice) and opt-in BBR on relay sockets
prs.protocol_changes: None on the wire. Relay server option `--tcp-congestion <name>` (env PB_MAPPER_TCP_CONGESTION, read at startup only), off by default, added to RelayServerOptions following its existing pattern without breaking public struct literals.
prs.design:
Why. (a) Linux restarts a TCP connection's congestion window from IW10 after an idle period (net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle = 1), so on relayed sessions the first scroll, window switch or IDR after a still period slow-starts: an estimated 100-400 ms more latency on that first burst over 50-150 ms legs. (b) With Cubic the relay->viewer leg's throughput ceiling is about 1.2 x MSS / (RTT x sqrt(p)): roughly 0.9 Mbit/s at 1% loss and 150 ms, below every preset's rate, so pace and bpf collapse on lossy cross-border and cellular legs; kernel BBR (mature BBRv1/v3 with a decaying bandwidth filter) is not limited by random loss.

1. docker/docker-compose.yml: `sysctls: net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle: 0` with a comment that it needs Linux 4.15+ and is namespaced to the container; a commented line for the congestion option.
2. scripts/install-server-github.sh and -gitee.sh: an opt-in prompt that writes /etc/sysctl.d/90-pb-mapper.conf.
3. pb-mapper-server on Linux, at startup: read /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_slow_start_after_idle; when 1, log one info event relay_tcp_idle_restart naming the fix (read-only).
4. `--tcp-congestion <name>`: on each accepted relay socket (connection.rs:117-121) set TCP_CONGESTION best effort (socket2's set_tcp_congestion); on EPERM or ENOENT log once with the fix (modprobe tcp_bbr plus net.ipv4.tcp_allowed_congestion_control, or CAP_NET_ADMIN in Docker). Only the relay's sending direction changes, which carries the relay->viewer video leg. Opt-in keeps zero cost by default; the fairness trade-off is the operator's choice.
5. Docs: an operator note in the user-guide pair (English and Chinese together) and DOCKER_README.md; CHANGELOG without figures.
prs.verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --workspace --all-features` (option parsing; the sysctl reader as a pure function over file content); `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`. CI nat-traversal.yml on Linux (`cargo build -p pb-mapper-cli --features port-mapping`, `sudo python3 scripts/test_nat_traversal.py --binary target/debug/pb-mapper`), node-e2e (CLI flags still parse).
prs.measurement: Device only, on a Linux relay (VM or the ubuntu CI runner with sudo): `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 50ms` with the relay on loopback; a testkit host and viewer (or transport_probe) idle 3 s, then ask for a keyframe (KeyframeReason::User): request-to-IDR-arrival time and cwnd from `ss -ti`, 20 rounds each at sysctl 1 and 0. BBR: `tc qdisc add dev <egress> root netem delay 75ms loss 0.1%` and `1%`, transport_probe and a desktop session through the relay, Cubic against BBR, 10 runs each: delivered Mbit/s, pace, sent_bitrate, IDR wait. Record under docs/benchmarks/<date>-relay-tcp/.
prs.verifiable_here: Build and unit tests here; every effect is Linux-device-only.

prs.name: disposable-frames
prs.title: Disposable (temporal-layer) frames: shed frames without an IDR on slow decoders and stop a room following its slowest viewer
prs.protocol_changes: None: both ends read NAL headers (nal_ref_idc / HEVC temporal ids). No helper change: the bit is derived from bytes the session already holds.
prs.design:
Why. A slow-decoder viewer (Linux software decode at 4K, older laptops) that falls behind today flushes its sink and forces an IDR on each backlog drop (slow_presenter recorded 3 drops and 3 requested IDRs in 10 s even before viewer-fps-cap), and in a multi-viewer room a drop at the hand-off forces an IDR for everyone while the shared stream follows the slowest viewer's pace (worker/capture.rs:224-227). Disposable (non-reference) frames can be shed without breaking the reference chain. Conditional on encoder compliance and efficiency, which Phase 0 measures.

Phase 0 (gate), on this Mac, ignored release tests in platform/macos/tests.rs reusing L's grain pattern and PSNR: (a) the default low-latency stream's share of non-reference units; (b) kVTCompressionPropertyKey_BaseLayerFrameRateFraction 0.5 with BaseLayerBitRateFraction 0.6: the disposable share and bits against a single layer at equal PSNR; (c) decode tolerance: drop the disposable units and decode the rest with VTDecompressionSession (decode feature for tests only), zero decode errors. Windows: a video_bench probe of CODECAPI_AVEncVideoTemporalLayerCount per vendor (device). Go on only for encoders with a disposable share >= 1/3 at a bitrate cost <= 5% at equal PSNR, or already present by default.
Phase 1: codec/annexb.rs marks `disposable` beside the IRAP check, carried on HostUnit and UnitMeta; Outgoing::push, when full, drops a disposable unit first without setting needs_keyframe; the viewer sink's backlog handling (episodes from viewer-fps-cap) drops queued disposable units before falling back to drop_to_idr; enable that drop on Media Foundation and GStreamer viewers only after a device check of each decoder.
Phase 2: rooms send base-layer units only to a viewer whose own pace is at most half the room's (session/sender.rs), and capture's minimum over viewers (worker/capture.rs:224-227) counts only viewers that keep up.
Zero cost: turn layers on by default only if Phase 0 shows they are free; otherwise only in rooms of two or more (encoder settings in platform/macos/encoder.rs on the submit thread and platform/windows/video/codec.rs).
Docs: room and sink sections; CHANGELOG with measured figures.
prs.verification: Here: `cargo fmt --all`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test -p pb-mapper-desktop --all-features` (disposable marking on VideoToolbox- and NVENC-made streams; Outgoing drops a disposable unit first without needs_keyframe; the sink drops disposable before drop_to_idr); `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`; `cargo run -p pb-mapper --features desktop --example desktop_loopback`. CI rust-windows-desktop, rust-macos-desktop, nat-traversal.yml.
prs.measurement: Phase 0 here: `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 video_toolbox_temporal_layers` (disposable share, bitrate cost at equal PSNR, decode errors after dropping). Phase 1, 3 release runs each before and after: slow_presenter with a synthetic encoder marking every other unit disposable (backlog_drops, keyframes_requested, presented fps); a two-viewer room with one viewer shaped to 1 Mbit/s (host keyframes and the fast viewer's received fps): `cargo test --release -p pb-mapper-desktop --lib -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1 slow_link`; host_send_bench allocations unchanged. Device: the MF temporal-layer probe; Linux GStreamer and Windows MF decode with disposable units dropped. Record under docs/benchmarks/.
prs.verifiable_here: Phase 0 for VideoToolbox and the pipeline logic are measurable here; Windows encoders and other decoders are device-only.
