plan.conflicts:
1. Present anchoring was proposed four times (R1, R3, R9, R10). One pacer rule is used, from R3 and R10 and the same as airhand host/pace.rs:34-50: an early window of P/4, creep of at most P/64, a 3/4-period floor. Its seam carries R9's Presented {at, presents}, so R9-M2 can lock on the present count.
- In process on both hosts: capture-anchored-pacing.
- The helper path: helper-push.
- R9-M2 is Windows-only (win-phase-locked-decimation). On the Mac, mac-capture-cadence already makes ScreenCaptureKit deliver every k-th vsync at an exact multiple, and the anchored pacer takes each picture on arrival.
- R1's `desktop_capture_wait` and R3/R10's `desktop_capture_pacing` are one event, desktop_capture_pacing.

2. Thread C seams are bundled into capture-anchored-pacing: submitted_picture, capture_poll, video_paused, and VideoSource presented, drain_poll, capture_poll, paused and retune, with PlatformBackend::configure_video calling retune. Without this, mac-capture-cadence (pause throttle, keep-capture), win-mf-output-events and helper-push would each touch the five #[deny(clippy::missing_trait_methods)] impls and native.rs. The defaults keep today's behaviour.

3. The VideoToolbox thread (R2-vt-submit-thread against R10-mac-vt-feeder): all VT calls run on one submit thread, as R10 asks. Two gates replace R10's newest-only mailbox replacement:
- in-flight >= 2 spends the tick, as R2-vt-inflight-two measured;
- a busy thread (a job in the mailbox, or inside a blocking call) leaves the tick armed (R2), so the freshest picture is taken when the thread frees up.
R10's switch rule counts these refused ticks instead of replacements. The thread inherits thread C's QoS class, so F (thread priority, withdrawn) is not reintroduced.

4. Rate models on the Mac. With Timestamp start (R9), standard rate control for H.265 (R10) sets AverageBitRate from encoder_bps under whichever model is in effect, and video_toolbox_120 verifies both. R8-receipt-rate-control's point (f), the DataRateLimits hold after a cut, moved into mac-vt-rate-control because the submit thread owns set_bitrate. receipt-rate-control does not depend on it formally; its fps shedding takes effect on Macs once the Timestamp start lands.

5. Throughput cap: R10's Backend::encoder_full and the helper's `full` field are dropped. After R3-need-input-armed, Submit::Full means only MAX_IN_FLIGHT (= ENCODER_DEPTH, which thread C sees as pending_video()) or a rare empty sample allocator. The serial case keeps its tick armed (Waiting) and builds no queue. Mac hosts are covered by their two-in-flight gate and the H.265 switch.

6. Still refinement (R3 against R9): one policy in codec/refine.rs. A burst needs a budget-sized fresh unit (R3) and 200 ms of stillness (R9). It stops after two near-empty repeats once REFINE_MIN have gone (R9), on a QP floor or a QP that stops falling (R3), or at the cap. The source is the held NV12 sample (R3), and the burst is enabled per vendor only from measurement.
- R9's typing soft tick is conditional on a device cost and would follow win-phase-locked-decimation, which owns the next pacer and helper change.
- R9's macOS re-send is R2-vt-resubmit-dropped.

7. fps cap (R5-fps-cap-capacity against R10-fps-cap-step-scale): the raise step is max(CAP_STEP x round(ceiling/30), ceil(0.25 x cap)) below the remembered capacity, plus R5's probing above it.
- R6-follow-window-refresh composes with both. Its `release` value replaces max_fps as 'no backlog cap', so a backlog recovery never clears the display limit.
- R10-win-viewer-exact-refresh feeds the same path: the Windows runner's exact refresh_hz is used at connect and on every metrics change (viewer-refresh).
- The Mac runner's window-screen refreshHz stat moved into viewer-decoder-stats.

8. keyframe_seq against drain-age backlog: with viewer-fps-cap, an age backlog keeps decoding queued units. after_seq is therefore set only when the sink is actually discarding P-frames (its wait_key), never for an age episode; otherwise the host would starve a draining viewer. This is why viewer-feedback touches sink.rs and depends on viewer-fps-cap.

9. Naming and merges:
- Arrival timestamps use the capability `arrival_time`; R8's `receipt_time` name is not used. The window's reverse term is R8's conservative minimum of the last 3 reverse queues.
- R8-keyframe-seq-skip rides in the same PR (viewer-feedback). It shares protocol.rs, outbound.rs, credit.rs and session.rs, and both are viewer-feedback fields.
- New capabilities: arrival_time, keyframe_seq, wheel_hires, relative_pointer, standby, av1. Every list stays within MAX_CAPABILITIES (16); the largest lists come to about 11 to 12. Each PR adds a test of the longest list sent.

10. AV1 is split into two PRs:
- av1-viewers: the protocol, every viewer, and a clip host that serves AV1. BackendCaps.av1 is ignored by the helper's From impls, so there is no bump.
- av1-windows-host: the MF encoder, a concurrent AV1 probe through a new provided Backend::probe_codec, the helper Encodes request, and the per-codec cache.
The probe cache is R3's host-side design with R9-M3's reboot-stable adapter key. Phase 1 of R9-win-viewer-d3d11va-hevc-av1 is R9-M1 (decoder-install-hints). Its phase 2, FFmpeg D3D11VA, is win-viewer-ffmpeg-decode, and its merge is gated on the owner's HEVC licensing decision.

11. Helper protocol: 10 is unreleased (v0.12.1 shipped 9). Six PRs change the helper wire and are ordered by depends_on, each bumping HELPER_PROTOCOL to master's value + 1 at merge, together with both .v<n> pipe names, readiness tests and the 'update the service' CHANGELOG line. The order is helper-probe-cache -> viewer-scroll -> helper-push -> relative-pointer -> av1-windows-host -> win-phase-locked-decimation. win-keep-awake avoids a helper change with a touch-driven keeper inside platform/windows, held while the video source is submitting, in process and in the worker alike. This also avoids oop/server.rs and timer.rs; the effect is unchanged, including release 2 s into a pause.

12. Linux module ABI: linux-gpu-convert, linux-presenting-gpu and av1-viewers each bump PB_VIDEO_MODULE_ABI at merge; file and symbol names stay. The decoder-install-hints Linux hint is derived in Dart from the existing `decoders` reply (h264 or h265 null), so it needs no module or runner change.

13. Native presenters:
- Grey still: mac-viewer-layer adds a `grey` method, because BackdropFilter cannot reach native content, and linux-video-plane implements it in the plane shader.
- One 'Sharpen enlarged picture' preference, introduced by mac-viewer-enhance, drives both Mac enhancement and Linux plane scaling. Linux downscale filtering is always on.
- Pixel snapping (viewer-pixel-snap) is applied to Flutter's transform, which both native presenters follow.
- Pointer features use a new `pb_mapper/desktop_pointer` runner channel created by native-cursor, extended by viewer-scroll (wheel_lines) and relative-pointer (pointer lock), so the desktop_video runners are not touched for them.

14. receipt-rate-control deviates from recorded decision D5 and CONTRACT-perf R13 (the probe owns fps and bitrate). The PR records the deviation in DECISIONS.md under the user's directive, as DECISIONS.md:1-5 requires. Its ship-order dependents host-direct-bbr and reconnect-start-rate follow it.

15. Ordering convention: any two PRs touching the same production source file (Rust, C++, Swift, C, Dart) are ordered by depends_on. This was checked mechanically over all 47 PRs with the script /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-lb7666--claude-spares-spare-vPIbq7/2de9709e-ea4b-442d-a692-7f9e8fd50cdd/scratchpad/notes/plan/dag.py, which finds 0 unordered overlaps.
- Registries are not treated as ordering constraints: CHANGELOG.md, docs/*.md and docs/benchmarks, l10n .arb files, `mod` declaration lines (lib.rs, codec/mod.rs), CMakeLists source lists, project.pbxproj, Cargo.toml feature lists, Cargo.lock, workflow apt package lists, and appended test cases in slow_link.rs, worker/tests.rs, platform/macos/tests.rs, viewer/tests.rs and ui/test. A PR appends there and resolves textual conflicts on rebase.
- Some edges exist only for shared-file order, not semantics: viewer-scroll after viewer-refresh (viewer/mod.rs); av1-viewers after standby-session and helper-push (protocol.rs, acceptor.rs, host.rs, proto.rs); relative-pointer after av1-viewers; encoder-throughput-cap before helper-push (worker/capture.rs); mac-vt-padded-capture after win-encoder-settings (codec/sps.rs, created there).
- The Windows host chain is serial on purpose: win-keep-awake -> win-mf-output-events -> win-encoder-settings -> win-capture-convert -> win-present-waiter -> win-hdr-desktop -> win-still-refinement -> av1-windows-host -> win-phase-locked-decimation. All of it shares video/mod.rs and compiles only on CI, so each step proves green before the next builds on it.

- Any Windows code (host, helper, runner): CI only.
- Linux: CI build and llvmpipe harness only.

- Everything else, including real VideoToolbox, the slow_link rigs, host_send_bench and the macOS app against desktop_ui_host, can be measured here.
